units.zh: 王導
units.en: Wang Dao
units.literal: Wang Dao.

units.zh: 王導，字茂弘，光祿大夫覽之孫也。
units.en: Wang Dao, whose courtesy name was Maohong, was the grandson of Wang Lan, who had held the office of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: Wang Dao, courtesy name Maohong, was the grandson of the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Wang Lan.

units.zh: 父裁，鎮軍司馬。
units.en: His father, Wang Cai, had served as Army Adjutant on the staff of the general titled "He Who Guards the Army."
units.literal: His father was Wang Cai, Army Adjutant of the General Who Guards the Army.

units.zh: 導少有風鑒，識量清遠。
units.en: Even as a young man, Wang Dao showed a gift for reading men; his judgment ran clear and deep.
units.literal: Dao from youth had insight into character and discernment; his capacity for judgment was limpid and far-reaching.

units.zh: 年十四，陳留高士張公見而奇之，謂其從兄敦曰：「此兒容貌志氣，將相之器也。」
units.en: When he was fourteen, a respected gentleman surnamed Zhang in Chenliu took note of him and pronounced him remarkable; Zhang said to Wang Dao's elder cousin Wang Dun, "In face and in spirit, this lad has the makings of a commander or a chief minister."
units.literal: At age fourteen, the eminent gentleman Zhang of Chenliu saw him and deemed him extraordinary; he said to Dao's elder cousin Dun, "This boy's appearance and resolve have the capacity of a general or minister."

units.zh: 初襲祖爵即丘子。
units.en: He first inherited his grandfather's noble title as Baron of Jiqiu.
units.literal: At first he inherited his grandfather's noble rank as Baron of Jiqiu.

units.zh: 司空劉實尋引爲東閣祭酒，遷秘書郎、太子舍人、尚書郎，並不行。
units.en: Minister of Works Liu Shi soon had him appointed Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion, then nominated him for Palace Secretary, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing—but Wang Dao declined every one of those appointments.
units.literal: The Minister of Works Liu Shi soon sponsored him as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion; he was transferred to Palace Secretary, Attendant in the Heir Apparent's Household, and Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, but he took none of these posts.

units.zh: 後參東海王越軍事。
units.en: He later joined the military secretariat of Sima Yue, the Prince of Donghai.
units.literal: Afterwards he served on the military staff of Prince Donghai, Sima Yue.

units.zh: 時元帝爲琅邪王，與導素相親善。
units.en: At the time, the future Emperor Yuan was Prince of Langye; he and Wang Dao had been close for years.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Yuan was Prince of Langye, and he and Dao had long been intimate and on good terms.

units.zh: 導知天下已亂，遂傾心推奉，潛有興復之志。
units.en: Wang Dao saw that the realm was coming apart; he committed himself to the prince and quietly nursed a plan to put the house of Jin back on its feet.
units.literal: Dao knew the realm was already in disorder; he therefore devoted his heart to supporting the prince and secretly harbored the ambition to revive and restore the dynasty.

units.zh: 帝亦雅相器重，契同友執。
units.en: The prince, for his part, held him in the highest regard; the two were as much confidants as liege and vassal.
units.literal: The prince also greatly esteemed him in return, and their bond was like that of friends who clasp hands as equals.

units.zh: 帝之在洛陽也，導每勸令之國。
units.en: When the prince was still in Luoyang, Wang Dao repeatedly urged him to take up residence in his assigned princedom.
units.literal: While the prince was in Luoyang, Dao often urged him to go to his princely fief.

units.zh: 會帝出鎮下邳，請導爲安東司馬，軍謀密策，知無不爲。
units.en: When the prince was sent to hold Xiapi, he asked to have Wang Dao as his Army Marshal of Peaceful East. For every design and every private counsel, Wang Dao gave all he had—nothing was beneath his effort.
units.literal: When the prince went out to garrison Xiapi, he requested Dao as Army Marshal of Peaceful East; for military plans and secret stratagems, there was nothing Dao would not do.

units.zh: 及徙鎮建康，呉人不附，居月餘，士庶莫有至者，導患之。
units.en: When the command shifted to Jiankang, the local elite of Wu held aloof. A month passed and still no notables or commoners had come forward, and Wang Dao grew anxious.
units.literal: When the headquarters were moved to Jiankang, the people of Wu did not attach themselves; after more than a month, neither gentry nor commoners had come, and Dao worried over it.

units.zh: 會敦來朝，導謂之曰：「琅邪王仁德雖厚，而名論猶輕。
units.en: When Wang Dun arrived for an audience, Wang Dao said to him, "The Prince of Langye is generous in humanity, but his name still carries little weight in the south.
units.literal: When Dun came to court, Dao said to him, "The Prince of Langye, though rich in benevolence and virtue, is still light in reputation and public esteem.

units.zh: 兄威風已振，宜有以匡濟者。」
units.en: You, elder brother, already command fear and respect; we need a gesture that will set things right."
units.literal: Elder brother, your awesome presence is already felt; there ought to be something by which to aid and deliver the situation."

units.zh: 會三月上巳，帝親觀禊，乘肩輿，具威儀，敦、導及諸名勝皆騎從。
units.en: It was the third month, the day of the spring purification. The prince went in person to the river rite, carried in a covered litter and escorted with full state, while Wang Dun, Wang Dao, and other leading men followed on horseback.
units.literal: It happened to be the third month's shangsi festival; the prince personally observed the river purification, riding in a shoulder-borne palanquin with full panoply of ceremony, while Dun, Dao, and all the eminent men followed on horseback.

units.zh: 呉人紀瞻、顧榮，皆江南之望，竊覘之，見其如此，咸驚懼，乃相率拜于道左。
units.en: Ji Zhan and Gu Rong of Wu were among the most influential men south of the Yangzi; watching discreetly, they were struck—and shaken—by the spectacle, and they stepped forward as one to bow along the roadside.
units.literal: The men of Wu, Ji Zhan and Gu Rong, were both paragons of the south; they spied on the procession from hiding, and when they saw it thus, all were awed and alarmed, and they together bowed on the left side of the road.

units.zh: 導因進計曰：「古之王者，莫不賓禮故老，存問風俗，虛己傾心，以招俊乂。
units.en: Wang Dao then offered a plan. "Rulers of old," he said, "always received local elders with ceremony, asked after local ways, and humbled themselves in order to win able men.
units.literal: Dao thereupon advanced a plan, saying, "The kings of old, without exception, treated venerable elders as honored guests, inquired into local customs, emptied themselves in humility, and opened their hearts to attract men of talent.

units.zh: 況天下喪亂，九州分裂，大業草創，急於得人者乎！
units.en: And all the more now—the empire is in ruins, the heartland broken apart, your enterprise barely launched, and nothing matters more than winning men of talent!
units.literal: How much more when the realm is lost to turmoil, the nine provinces split apart, the great enterprise only just begun, and the need for capable men is urgent!

units.zh: 顧榮、賀循，此土之望，未若引之以結人心。
units.en: Gu Rong and He Xun are the great names here; bring them in, and you will tie the region's loyalty to you.
units.literal: Gu Rong and He Xun are the luminaries of this land; nothing would be better than to draw them in to bind the people's hearts.

units.zh: 二子既至，則無不來矣。」
units.en: Once those two appear at court, the rest will follow of their own accord."
units.literal: Once those two arrive, there will be none who do not come."

units.zh: 帝乃使導躬造循、榮，二人皆應命而至，由是呉會風靡，百姓歸心焉。
units.en: The prince accordingly sent Wang Dao in person to visit He Xun and Gu Rong; both accepted his invitation at once. From that moment the southeast rallied behind him, and popular allegiance swung his way.
units.literal: The prince then sent Dao himself to call on He Xun and Gu Rong; both responded to the summons and came. Thereupon Wu and Kuaiji were swept along as if by wind, and the common people turned their hearts to him.

units.zh: 自此之後，漸相崇奉，君臣之禮始定。
units.en: After that, respect for the prince deepened step by step, and something like a settled relationship between sovereign and subject began to take shape.
units.literal: From this time onward, they gradually honored and served him, and the rites between lord and minister were at last established.

units.zh: 俄而洛京傾覆，中州士女避亂江左者十六七，導勸帝收其賢人君子，與之圖事。
units.en: When Luoyang collapsed, well over half the gentry and families of the north streamed across the Yangzi for refuge; Wang Dao urged the prince to recruit their best men and govern with them at his side.
units.literal: Soon the capital Luoyang fell; sixty or seventy percent of gentlemen and ladies of the central plain fled the turmoil to the left bank of the Yangzi, and Dao urged the prince to gather their worthy men and gentlemen of virtue and plan affairs with them.

units.zh: 時荊揚晏安，戸口殷實，導爲政務在清靜，每勸帝克己勵節，匡主寧邦。
units.en: Jingzhou and Yangzhou were calm then, the registers full and the land rich. Wang Dao ran government on light touch—he constantly urged the emperor to discipline himself, steel his resolve, support his sovereign, and bring peace to the realm.
units.literal: At that time Jing and Yang were peaceful; households were numerous and prosperous. Dao's governance aimed at clarity and quiet; he often urged the prince to restrain himself and steel his integrity, to aid his lord and settle the state.

units.zh: 於是尤見委杖，情好日隆，朝野傾心，號爲「仲父」。
units.en: He was leaned on as never before; trust between him and the throne deepened by the day, and everyone from the court outward looked to him—the people called him "the Zhongfu," their second father.
units.literal: Thereupon he was especially entrusted and relied upon; their affection grew daily; court and countryside bent their hearts to him, and he was styled "Second Father."

units.zh: 帝嘗從容謂導曰：「卿，吾之蕭何也。」
units.en: Once the emperor said to Wang Dao, almost casually, "You are my Xiao He."
units.literal: The emperor once said unhurriedly to Dao, "You are my Xiao He."

units.zh: 對曰：「昔秦爲無道，百姓厭亂，巨猾陵暴，人懷漢德，革命反正，易以爲功。
units.en: Wang Dao answered, "When Qin ruled without principle, the people had had enough of chaos; powerful brutes ran riot; everyone looked to the virtue of Han. Replacing the dynasty and putting things right could be done almost overnight.
units.literal: He replied, "In former times Qin practiced cruelty; the hundred clans wearied of turmoil; great villains rampaged; men cherished Han's virtue; the mandate changed and order was restored—success came easily.

units.zh: 自魏氏以來，迄于太康之際，公卿世族，豪侈相高，政教陵遲，不遵法度，群公卿士，皆饜於安息，遂使人乘釁，有虧至道。
units.en: From Wei through the Taikang years, great families outdid one another in ostentation; government grew slack and law meant little; officials grew fat on ease until rebels found their opening—that is how the supreme Way was betrayed.
units.literal: From the time of Wei down to the Taikang era, dukes and ministers and hereditary great clans vied in luxury and extravagance; governance and instruction declined and did not observe statutes and norms; hosts of dukes, ministers, and gentlemen were sated with peace and ease, whereupon men exploited openings and inflicted loss upon the utmost Way.

units.zh: 然否終斯泰，天道之常。
units.en: Still, bad seasons turn; that is how Heaven works.
units.literal: Yet adversity ends and thus comes peace—such is the constant of Heaven's way.

units.zh: 大王方立命世之勳，一匡九合，管仲、樂毅，於是乎在，豈區區國臣所可擬議！
units.en: Your Highness is building the achievement that will steady an age—uniting the realm as Guan Zhong and Yue Yi once did. No ordinary courtier belongs in the same sentence.
units.literal: Your Highness is now founding merit that steadies the age, rectifying all within and uniting the nine regions—there indeed stand Guan Zhong and Yue Yi; how could they be matched by some petty minister of state!

units.zh: 願深弘神慮，廣擇良能。
units.en: Broaden your counsel and cast the net wide for capable men.
units.literal: I pray you broaden your divine deliberations and widely select the able and good.

units.zh: 顧榮、賀循、紀贍、周圮皆南土之秀，願盡優禮，則天下安矣。」
units.en: Gu Rong, He Xun, Ji Zhan, and Zhou Qi are the pick of the south; honor them generously, and the world will settle."
units.literal: Gu Rong, He Xun, Ji Zhan, and Zhou Qi are all luminaries of the southern lands; I pray you extend them full courteous treatment, and then the realm will be at peace."

units.zh: 帝納焉。
units.en: The emperor took his advice.
units.literal: The emperor accepted this.

units.zh: 永嘉末，遷丹陽太守，加輔國將軍。
units.en: Late in the Yongjia reign he was made governor of Danyang and appointed General Who Supports the State.
units.literal: At the end of the Yongjia era, he was transferred to Governor of Danyang and given the additional title General Who Supports the State.

units.zh: 導上箋曰：「昔魏武，達政之主也；
units.en: Wang Dao sent up a memorial: "Emperor Wu of Wei understood how to govern;
units.literal: Dao submitted a note, saying, "In former times Emperor Wu of Wei was a ruler who understood governance;

units.zh: 荀文若，功臣之最也，封不過亭侯。
units.en: yet even Xun Yu, his greatest servant, was ennobled no higher than Village Marquis.
units.literal: Xun Wenruo was foremost among meritorious servants, yet his enfeoffment went no higher than Village Marquis.

units.zh: 倉舒，愛子之寵，贈不過別部司馬。
units.en: His beloved son Cangshu—posthumous rank stopped at Major of a Separate Command.
units.literal: Cangshu, a beloved son's favor, received posthumous rank no higher than Major of a Separate Command.

units.zh: 以此格萬物，得不局跡乎！
units.en: If that was his standard for everyone, small wonder offices stayed within bounds!
units.literal: Using this as the measure for all things—could one not be cramped and constrained!

units.zh: 今者臨郡，不問賢愚豪賤，皆加重號，輒有鼓蓋，動見相准。
units.en: Today anyone who takes a county post—wise or dull, highborn or low—walks away with a grand title, drums and canopy and all, each trying to keep up with the next.
units.literal: Now when one presides over a commandery, without distinguishing worthy from foolish, eminent from humble, all alike receive inflated titles, invariably with drum and canopy; every move is matched against another.

units.zh: 時有不得者，或爲恥辱。
units.en: Anyone left out feels publicly shamed.
units.literal: Those who at times do not obtain such things sometimes regard it as shame and humiliation.

units.zh: 天官混雜，朝望頹毀。
units.en: Ranks are handed out indiscriminately, and the court's dignity has collapsed.
units.literal: Heaven's offices are mixed and confused; court prestige is ruined and destroyed.

units.zh: 導忝荷重任，不能崇浚山海，而開導亂源，饕竊名位，取紊彝典，謹送鼓蓋加崇之物，請從導始。
units.en: I carry a heavy burden unworthily: instead of elevating the office I have cheapened it—grasping at rank and upsetting precedent. I therefore send back the drums, canopy, and other marks of favor; let the retrenchment begin with me.
units.literal: Dao shamefully bears a heavy charge; unable to deepen and broaden like mountains and seas, I have opened the source of disorder, greedily usurping titles and stations, taking and disordering the constant canons; I respectfully return the objects of drum and canopy and added honors—let it begin with Dao.

units.zh: 庶令雅俗區別，群望無惑。」
units.en: Perhaps that will separate true distinction from mere display and spare the court further embarrassment."
units.literal: Perhaps thereby refined and common may be distinguished, and the expectations of the multitude will not be confused."

units.zh: 帝下令曰：「導德重勳高，孤所深倚，誠宜表彰殊禮。
units.en: The emperor replied with an edict: "Wang Dao's virtue and record are immense; I lean on him heavily—he deserves special recognition.
units.literal: The emperor issued an order, saying, "Dao's virtue is weighty and his merit high; I deeply rely on him; he truly ought to be marked out with special rites of honor.

units.zh: 而更約己沖心，進思盡誠，以身率眾，宜順其雅志，式允開塞之機。」
units.en: Yet he insists on modesty, gives his counsel in good faith, and leads by example—grant him what he asks; it is the right way to open or close a policy."
units.literal: Yet further he restrains himself with a humble heart, advances his thinking with utmost sincerity, and leads the multitude by his person—one ought to comply with his refined intent and thereby fulfill the pivot that opens and closes."

units.zh: 拜甯遠將軍，尋加振威將軍。
units.en: He received the title General Who Pacifies the Distance, then shortly afterward General Who Rouses Might.
units.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance; soon after he was given the additional title General Who Rouses Might.

units.zh: 湣帝即位，征吏部郎，不拜。
units.en: When Emperor Min came to the throne, Wang Dao was called to serve as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel; he declined.
units.literal: When Emperor Min mounted the throne, Dao was summoned as Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel; he did not take up the post.

units.zh: 晉國既建，以導爲丞相軍諮祭酒。
units.en: Once the Jin domain was founded, Wang Dao was appointed Libationer for Army Consultation under the chancellor.
units.literal: When the state of Jin was established, Dao was made Libationer for Army Consultation under the Chancellor.

units.zh: 桓彝初過江，見朝廷微弱，謂周顗曰：「我以中州多故，來此欲求全活，而寡弱如此，將何以濟！」
units.en: When Huan Yi first crossed the river, he found the court alarmingly weak. He said to Zhou Yi, "I left the north for turmoil's sake, hoping only to survive—but if power here is this slight, what hope is there?"
units.literal: When Huan Yi first crossed the Yangzi, he saw the court was feeble; he said to Zhou Yi, "Because the central plain had many troubles, I came here wishing to preserve my life whole, yet it is so thin and weak—how shall we be delivered!"

units.zh: 憂懼不樂。
units.en: He grew anxious and miserable.
units.literal: He was anxious and fearful and not happy.

units.zh: 往見導，極談世事，還，謂顗曰：「向見管夷吾，無復憂矣。」
units.en: He went to Wang Dao and talked at length about the state of the realm. When he came back he told Zhou Yi, "I have seen our Guan Zhong—I have nothing left to fear."
units.literal: He went to see Dao and exhaustively discussed affairs of the age; returning, he said to Yi, "Just now I saw Guan Yiwu—there is no more worry."

units.zh: 過江人士，每至暇日，相要出新亭飲宴。
units.en: Northerners who had crossed the river would meet on free days and arrange outings to Xinting for drinking parties.
units.literal: Men who had crossed the Yangzi, whenever they reached leisure days, invited one another to go out to Xinting to drink and feast.

units.zh: 周顗中坐而歎曰：「風景不殊，舉目有江河之異。」
units.en: Once Zhou Yi, seated among them, sighed and said, "The hills and streams look the same—but we have crossed the great river into exile."
units.literal: Zhou Yi, seated in the midst, sighed and said, "The scenery is no different, yet lifting the eyes there is the difference of the rivers."

units.zh: 皆相視流涕。
units.en: They exchanged glances and wept.
units.literal: All looked at one another and wept.

units.zh: 惟導愀然變色曰：「當共戮力王室，克復神州，何至作楚囚相對泣邪！」
units.en: Only Wang Dao's face darkened. "We should join forces for the house of Jin and win back the heartland," he said. "Are we to cry together like prisoners of Chu?"
units.literal: Only Dao, sternly changing color, said, "We ought together to devote our strength to the royal house, to recover the divine land—how could we reach the point of facing one another weeping like captives of Chu!"

units.zh: 眾收淚而謝之。
units.en: Ashamed, they dried their eyes and apologized.
units.literal: The multitude wiped their tears and apologized to him.

units.zh: 俄拜右將軍、揚州刺史、監江南諸軍事，遷驃騎將軍，加散騎常侍、都督中外諸軍、領中書監、録尚書事、假節，刺史如故。
units.en: Shortly afterward he was named General of the Right, inspector of Yangzhou, and supervisor of Jiangnan military affairs; he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, given the additional posts of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and commander-in-chief of forces within and without, headed the palace secretariat and recorded edicts for the Masters of Writing, received the ceremonial credentials—and kept his provincial post.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Right, Inspector of Yang Province, and Supervisor of Military Affairs South of the Yangzi; he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry and given the additional posts Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of All Military Forces Within and Without, concurrent Supervisor of the Palace Writers, and Recorder of Masters-of-Writing Affairs, with credential staff; his inspector post remained as before.

units.zh: 導以敦統六州，固辭中外都督。
units.en: Because Wang Dun already controlled six provinces, Wang Dao firmly declined the joint inner-and-outer command.
units.literal: Because Dun commanded six provinces, Dao firmly declined the command of forces within and without.

units.zh: 後坐事除節。
units.en: Later an incident cost him his ceremonial staff.
units.literal: Later, because of an affair, he was stripped of his staff of authority.

units.zh: 于時軍旅不息，學校未修，導上書曰：
units.en: War dragged on while schools lay neglected; Wang Dao submitted a memorial:
units.literal: At that time armies did not cease and schools were not repaired; Dao submitted a memorial, saying:

units.zh: :　　夫風化之本在於正人倫，人倫之正存乎設庠序。
units.en: To shift customs you must first set human relations right; to set relations right you must found schools.
units.literal: The root of transforming customs lies in rectifying human relationships; the rectification of human relationships resides in establishing schools.

units.zh: 庠序設，五教明，德禮洽通，彝倫攸敘，而有恥且格，父子兄弟夫婦長幼之序順，而君臣之義固矣。
units.en: Schools clarify the five moral teachings, knit virtue and ritual together, and give society its proper shape—shame keeps people honest; fathers and sons, husbands and wives, elders and juniors fall into place, and the bond between ruler and minister holds firm.
units.literal: When schools are established, the five teachings are illumined; virtue and ritual unite and penetrate; the constant human relationships are thereby ordered, and there is shame and correction; the order of father and son, elder and younger brothers, husband and wife, elder and younger is smooth, and the righteousness of lord and minister is firm.

units.zh: 《易》所謂「正家而天下定」者也。
units.en: This is the Changes teaching: "Order the household and the realm finds peace."
units.literal: This is what the Changes calls "rectifying the family and thereby settling the realm."

units.zh: 故聖王蒙以養正，少而教之，使化沾肌骨，習以成性，遷善遠罪而不自知，行成德立，然後裁之以位。
units.en: The sage kings nurtured young minds early so moral teaching sank into the bone; habit became character, people turned from wrong almost without thinking, and only when conduct proved sound did they award office.
units.literal: Therefore the sage kings used the hexagram Meng to nurture correctness; they instructed from youth so that transformation soaked into muscle and bone and habit became nature; they shifted toward goodness and kept distant from crime without self-awareness; conduct was accomplished and virtue established, and only afterward did they assign positions according to capacity.

units.zh: 雖王之世子，猶與國子齒，使知道而後貴。
units.en: Even a crown prince studied beside other cadets so that he learned the Way before he learned rank.
units.literal: Even the heir of a king still ranked with the sons of state, making them understand the Way and only then honor.

units.zh: 其取才用士，咸先本之於學。
units.en: Talent always came out of the schools first.
units.literal: In selecting talent and employing gentlemen, they all first rooted it in learning.

units.zh: 故《周禮》，卿大夫獻賢能之書于王，王拜而受之，所以尊道而貴士也。
units.en: Hence the Zhou ritual: ministers forwarded rosters of worthy men to the throne, and the king bowed as he took them—that was respect for learning and for scholars.
units.literal: Therefore in the Rites of Zhou, ministers and great officers presented the documents on worthy and capable men to the king, and the king bowed and received them—this was how they honored the Way and esteemed gentlemen.

units.zh: 人知士之貴由道存，則退而修其身以及家，正其家以及鄕，學於鄕以登朝，反本復始，各求諸己，敦樸之業著，浮偽之競息，教使然也。
units.en: When people saw that true standing rested on moral cultivation, they minded their own conduct, ordered their households, studied in their districts, and carried those lessons to court—everyone looked inward, simplicity flourished, and hollow ambition faded. That is what teaching achieves.
units.literal: When men knew that the honor of gentlemen resides in the Way's preservation, then they withdrew and cultivated their persons extending to their families, rectified their families extending to their villages, studied in their villages to ascend to court, returned to the root and restored the beginning, each seeking it in himself; the enterprise of honest simplicity was manifest and the rivalry of empty falsity rested—such was the effect of instruction.

units.zh: 故以之事君則忠，用之蒞下則仁。
units.en: Such men serve their sovereign with loyalty and rule others with humanity.
units.literal: Therefore used to serve the lord, there is loyalty; used to oversee those below, there is benevolence.

units.zh: 孟軻所謂「未有仁而遺其親，義而後其君者也」。
units.en: Mencius put it this way: "No humane man abandons his parents; no dutiful man leaves his lord behind."
units.literal: This is what Meng Ke called "there has never been one benevolent who neglected his kin, nor one righteous who put his lord second."

units.zh: :　　自頃皇綱失統，頌聲不興，於今將二紀矣。
units.en: For years the imperial order has frayed and the classic hymns have fallen silent—almost twenty-four years now.
units.literal: From recent times the imperial net has lost its cords; songs of praise have not risen; down to now it is nearly two twelve-year cycles.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「三年不爲禮，禮必壞；
units.en: The classics warn: "neglect ritual for three years and ritual collapses;
units.literal: The Tradition says, "If for three years one does not practice ritual, ritual must decay;

units.zh: 三年不爲樂，樂必崩。」
units.en: neglect music for three years and music falls apart."
units.literal: if for three years one does not practice music, music must collapse."

units.zh: 而況如此之久乎！
units.en: What then after decades?
units.literal: How much more when it has been this long!"

units.zh: 先進忘揖讓之容，後生惟金鼓是聞，干戈日尋，俎豆不設，先王之道彌遠，華偽之俗遂滋，非所以端本靖末之謂也。
units.en: Elders no longer remember courtesy; youths hear only war drums; armies march while sacrifices go unattended; the ancient kings feel farther away than ever and vain display spreads. That is no way to heal root and branch.
units.literal: The older generation forgets the deportment of bowing and yielding; the younger generation hears only gongs and drums; weapons are sought daily; sacrificial stands and vessels are not set out; the Way of the former kings grows ever more distant; ostentatious falsity flourishes—this is not what is called rectifying the root and pacifying the branches."

units.zh: 殿下以命世之資，屬陽九之運，禮樂征伐，翼成中興。
units.en: Your Highness was born for this age and faces the ninth yang cycle—ritual, music, and arms alike serve the revival.
units.literal: Your Highness, with endowment that commands the age, stands in the fortune of the yang nine; ritual, music, punitive expeditions, and attacks wing-like accomplish restoration."

units.zh: 誠宜經綸稽古，建明學業，以訓後生，漸之教義，使文武之道墜而復興，俎豆之儀幽而更彰。
units.en: You should look to antiquity, reopen the schools, train the young in stages, and restore both civil learning and military discipline—bring back the rites that once seemed lost.
units.literal: Truly one ought to plan and organize by examining antiquity, establish and clarify academic studies, to instruct the younger generation, gradually instill teaching and righteousness, cause the Way of civil and military that had fallen to revive again, and make the rites of stands and vessels that were hidden shine forth once more."

units.zh: 方今戎虜扇熾，國恥未雪，忠臣義夫所以扼腕拊心。
units.en: Barbarians still ravage the north and national shame hangs open—every loyal heart clenches in grief.
units.literal: Now barbarian enemies fan the flames; national shame is not yet avenged—this is why loyal ministers and righteous husbands gnash wrists and strike their hearts."

units.zh: 苟禮儀膠固，淳風漸著，則化之所感者深而德之所被者大。
units.en: Fix ritual firmly and let honest custom grow—the deeper the transformation spreads, the broader your virtue will reach.
units.literal: If ritual and propriety are firmly fixed and honest customs gradually appear, then what transformation touches will be deep and what virtue overspreads will be great."

units.zh: 使帝典闕而復補，皇綱弛而更張，獸心革面，饕餮檢情，揖讓而服四夷，緩帶而天下從。
units.en: Patch what the canons have lost, tighten what the dynastic net has let slip; turn savage temperaments, curb greedy wills; win the border peoples with courtesy and the realm with calm authority.
units.literal: Cause the imperial canons that were lacking to be restored, the royal net that was slack to be restrung; brutal hearts to change their faces, rapacious appetites to restrain their passions; with bowing and yielding to subdue the four barbarians, with loose belt to have the realm follow."

units.zh: 得乎其道，豈難也哉！
units.en: Master that path and the rest is not hard.
units.literal: If one obtains this Way, how could it be difficult!"

units.zh: 故有虞舞干戚而化三苗，魯僖作泮宮而服淮夷。
units.en: Shun turned the Sanmiao with ritual dance; Duke Xi of Lu bent the Huai tribes by founding the southern school.
units.literal: Therefore Shun of Youyu danced with shield and axe and transformed the Sanmiao; Duke Xi of Lu built the Pan Palace and brought the Huai Yi to submission."

units.zh: 桓文之霸，皆先教而後戰。
units.en: Even Duke Huan and Duke Wen taught before they struck.
units.literal: The hegemony of Huan and Wen both first taught and afterward fought."

units.zh: 今若聿遵前典，興復道教，擇朝之子弟併入於學，選明博修禮之士而爲之師，化成俗定，莫尚於斯。
units.en: Follow the old statutes, revive moral education, enroll your kinsmen in the schools, and appoint learned ritualists as teachers—nothing does more to settle custom and complete the transformation.
units.literal: Now if we earnestly follow the former canons, revive and restore the teaching of the Way, select the sons and younger brothers of the court and send them together into learning, choose enlightened, learned men cultivated in ritual to be their teachers—transformation will be achieved and customs settled; nothing is higher than this."

units.zh: 帝甚納之。
units.en: The emperor embraced the proposal wholeheartedly.
units.literal: The emperor greatly accepted it.

units.zh: 及帝登尊號，百官陪列，命導升御床共坐。
units.en: When the emperor assumed the throne, the whole court stood in attendance as he told Wang Dao to join him on the imperial couch.
units.literal: When the emperor ascended the honored title, the hundred officials attending in ranks, he ordered Dao to ascend the imperial couch and sit together.

units.zh: 導固辭，至於三四，曰：「若太陽下同萬物，蒼生何由仰照！」
units.en: Wang Dao refused again and again—three or four rounds—and said, "If the sun stooped to share a seat with everything beneath it, how could living things feel its light?"
units.literal: Dao firmly declined, to the point of three or four times, saying, "If the great sun dwelt together with the myriad things, by what means would the black-haired folk look up to its radiance!"

units.zh: 帝乃止。
units.en: The emperor dropped the idea.
units.literal: The emperor then desisted.

units.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。
units.en: He was promoted to supreme commander with honors equal to the Three Senior Offices.
units.literal: He was promoted to Supreme General Who Inspires Awe and granted equivalence to the Three Offices.

units.zh: 以討華軼功，封武岡侯。
units.en: His victory over Hua Yi earned him the marquisate of Wugang.
units.literal: For merit in campaigning against Hua Yi, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wugang.

units.zh: 進位侍中、司空、假節、録尚書，領中書監。
units.en: He rose to palace attendant, minister of works, recorder of Masters of Writing, and chief of the palace secretariat, with full credentials.
units.literal: He advanced to Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, credential staff, Recorder of Masters-of-Writing Affairs, and concurrent Supervisor of the Palace Writers.

units.zh: 會太山太守徐龕反，帝訪可以鎮撫河南者，導舉太子左衞率羊鑒。
units.en: When Taishan prefect Xu Kan rose in revolt, the emperor asked who could stabilize the Henan region; Wang Dao recommended Yang Jian, colonel of the heir apparent's left guard.
units.literal: When Taishan Prefect Xu Kan rebelled, the emperor sought someone who could pacify and comfort the region south of the Yellow River; Dao recommended Colonel of the Left Palace Guards for the Heir Apparent, Yang Jian.

units.zh: 既而鑒敗，抵罪。
units.en: Yang Jian was beaten in the field and incurred punishment.
units.literal: Soon Jian was defeated and incurred punishment.

units.zh: 導上疏曰：「徐龕叛戾，久稽天誅，臣創議征討，調舉羊鑒。
units.en: Wang Dao memorialized: "Xu Kan has defied the throne far too long. I urged the campaign and put forward Yang Jian.
units.literal: Dao submitted a memorial, saying, "Xu Kan is rebellious and violent; long has he delayed Heaven's punishment; your servant initiated the plan for campaigning and punitive expedition and nominated Yang Jian.

units.zh: 鑒暗懦覆師，有司極法。
units.en: He proved timid and lost the army; justice demanded the severest penalty.
units.literal: Jian was dim-witted and cowardly and overturned the army; the relevant offices applied the utmost law.

units.zh: 聖恩降天地之施，全其首領。
units.en: Your mercy spared his life.
units.literal: The sagely grace lowered Heaven-and-earth's bounty and preserved his head and neck.

units.zh: 然臣受重任，總録機衡，使三軍挫衄，臣之責也。
units.en: Yet I bore chief responsibility at court; when the armies suffered defeat, the fault is mine.
units.literal: Yet your servant received a heavy charge and overall recorded the pivot balances, causing the three armies to suffer setback and defeat—it is your servant's responsibility.

units.zh: 乞自貶黜，以穆朝倫。」
units.en: I ask to be stripped of rank myself so that justice may satisfy the court."
units.literal: I beg to demote and dismiss myself, so as to harmonize court norms."

units.zh: 詔不許。
units.en: The emperor would not hear of it.
units.literal: An edict disallowed it.

units.zh: 尋代賀循領太子太傅。
units.en: He soon succeeded He Xun as grand tutor to the crown prince.
units.literal: Soon he replaced He Xun as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 時中興草創，未置史官，導始啟立，於是典籍頗具。
units.en: The revival regime was still taking shape and had no official historians until Wang Dao petitioned to create the office; after that, court archives began to look like a real library.
units.literal: At that time the restoration was newly begun and no historiographers had yet been installed; Dao first proposed establishing them, whereupon canonical records became fairly complete.

units.zh: 時孝懷太子爲胡所害，始奉諱，有司奏天子三朝舉哀，群臣一哭而已。
units.en: When news arrived that Crown Prince Xiaohuai had been murdered by the Hu, the court began observing death taboos; the ministry proposed three audiences for the emperor's lament while officials might offer only a single collective weeping.
units.literal: At that time Crown Prince Xiaohuai had been killed by the Hu; they began to observe the taboo on his name, and the relevant offices memorialized that for three court sessions the Son of Heaven should express grief, while host of ministers weep only once.

units.zh: 導以爲皇太子副貳宸極，普天有情，宜同三朝之哀。
units.en: Wang Dao argued that a crown prince stands second only to the throne: the whole realm mourns him; mourning should match the three audiences proposed for the monarch.
units.literal: Dao held that the crown prince is deputy to the Pole Star throne; all under Heaven has feeling; it is fitting to share the grief of three audiences.

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The court agreed.
units.literal: They followed him.

units.zh: 及劉隗用事，導漸見疏遠，任真推分，澹如也。
units.en: Once Liu Wei dominated policy, Wang Dao found himself sidelined; he simply remained himself, accepted his reduced role, and showed no resentment.
units.literal: When Liu Wei came to power, Dao was gradually seen as estranged; he trusted what was genuine and yielded to his allotted portion, placid as ever.

units.zh: 有識咸稱導善處興廢焉。
units.en: Thoughtful observers agreed that Wang Dao knew how to endure fortune and misfortune alike.
units.literal: Men of insight all praised Dao as skilled in dwelling amid rise and ruin.

units.zh: 王敦之反也，劉隗勸帝悉誅王氏，論者爲之危心。
units.en: When Wang Dun rose in revolt, Liu Wei pressed the emperor to wipe out the whole Wang family; observers feared the worst for them.
units.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled, Liu Wei urged the emperor to execute the entire Wang clan; commentators were fearful for them.

units.zh: 導率群從昆弟子侄二十餘人，每旦詣台待罪。
units.en: Every morning Wang Dao presented himself at the palace with more than twenty kinsmen—cousins, nephews, and grandsons—to answer for the rebellion.
units.literal: Dao led more than twenty elder and younger male cousins, nephews, and grand-nephews of his lineage; each dawn they went to the terrace to await punishment.

units.zh: 帝以導忠節有素，特還朝服，召見之。
units.en: The emperor, knowing Wang Dao's loyalty of old, restored his court dress and received him in audience.
units.literal: Because the emperor considered Dao's loyalty and integrity long-standing, he specially returned court robes and summoned him to audience.

units.zh: 導稽首謝曰：「逆臣賊子，何世無之，豈意今者近出臣族！」
units.en: Wang Dao kowtowed and said, "Traitors appear in every age—yet who could have thought they would spring from my own family?"
units.literal: Dao knocked his head and apologized, saying, "Rebellious ministers and unfilial sons—what age lacks them? How could I have expected that today they should emerge so close as my own clan!"

units.zh: 帝跣而執之曰：「茂弘，方托百里之命於卿，是何言邪！」
units.en: The emperor slipped off his shoes, took Wang Dao by the hand, and said, "Maohong, I am staking the dynasty on you—how can you speak like that?"
units.literal: The emperor, barefoot, seized his hand and said, "Maohong, I am just now entrusting the fate of the realm to you—what words are these!"

units.zh: 乃詔曰：「導以大義滅親，可以吾爲安東時節假之。」
units.en: An edict followed: "Wang Dao has put duty above clan; grant him the same ceremonial credentials I bore as General of Peaceful East."
units.literal: Thereupon an edict declared: "Dao, by great righteousness destroying kinship, may be lent the credential staff I held as General of Peaceful East."

units.zh: 及敦得志，加導守尚書令。
units.en: Once Wang Dun had his way, Wang Dao was appointed acting director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: When Dun achieved his aims, Dao was additionally given acting Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 初，西都覆沒，海內思主，群臣及四方並勸進於帝。
units.en: After Chang'an fell, the realm hungered for a sovereign; officials and regional powers alike pressed the prince to take the throne.
units.literal: At first, when the western capital was overthrown and lost, within the seas men yearned for a ruler; hosts of ministers and the four quarters together urged advancement upon the emperor.

units.zh: 時王氏強盛，有專天下之心，敦憚帝賢明，欲更議所立，導固爭乃止。
units.en: The Wang family was strong enough to dominate the state; Wang Dun feared an able emperor and wanted another candidate, but Wang Dao argued him down.
units.literal: At that time the Wang clan was powerful and had a mind to monopolize the realm; Dun feared the emperor's sagacity and wished to reopen deliberation on whom to establish, but Dao firmly argued and it stopped.

units.zh: 及此役也，敦謂導曰：「不從吾言，幾致覆族。」
units.en: Afterward Wang Dun told Wang Dao, "If you had defied me, our whole clan would nearly have been destroyed."
units.literal: When this campaign occurred, Dun said to Dao, "Had you not followed my words, it would nearly have brought destruction on the clan."

units.zh: 導猶執正議，敦無以能奪。
units.en: Wang Dao still held to principle, and Wang Dun could not shake him.
units.literal: Dao still upheld correct counsel; Dun had no means to wrest it away.

units.zh: 自漢魏已來，賜諡多由封爵，雖位通德重，先無爵者，例不加諡。
units.en: Since Han and Wei times, posthumous names usually tracked noble titles—high office alone was not enough without a prior peerage.
units.literal: From Han and Wei onward, bestowed posthumous titles mostly followed enfeoffed noble ranks; although rank matched virtue's weight, if there had previously been no noble rank, by precedent no posthumous title was added.

units.zh: 導乃上疏，稱「武官有爵必諡，卿校常伯無爵不諡，甚失制度之本意也」。
units.en: Wang Dao memorialized, saying, "When military officers with titles receive posthumous honors but civil ministers without fiefs do not, the system misses its intended purpose."
units.literal: Dao then submitted a memorial, stating, "Military officers if they have noble rank invariably receive posthumous titles; ministers and regular elders without noble rank receive none—this greatly misses the root intention of the institutions."

units.zh: 從之。
units.en: The emperor accepted his argument.
units.literal: They followed him.

units.zh: 自後公卿無爵而諡，導所議也。
units.en: Henceforth ministers could earn posthumous names without holding a noble rank—an innovation Wang Dao had urged.
units.literal: Afterward dukes and ministers without noble rank receiving posthumous titles was due to Dao's proposal.

units.zh: 初，帝愛琅邪王裒，將有奪嫡之議，以問導。
units.en: The emperor favored Prince Sima Pou of Langye and toyed with replacing the heir; he asked Wang Dao what he thought.
units.literal: At first the emperor loved Prince Langye, Sima Pou, and there was discussion of displacing the heir apparent; he consulted Dao.

units.zh: 導曰：「夫立子以長，且紹又賢，不宜改革。」
units.en: Wang Dao replied, "Succession belongs to the eldest son, and Sima Shao is worthy; you should not change course."
units.literal: Dao said, "In establishing sons one relies on seniority; moreover Shao is again worthy; it is not fitting to alter this."

units.zh: 帝猶疑之。
units.en: The emperor remained unconvinced.
units.literal: The emperor still doubted.

units.zh: 導日夕陳諫，故太子卒定。
units.en: Wang Dao argued day and night until the succession stayed with the original heir.
units.literal: Dao remonstrated morning and evening; therefore the crown prince was finally settled.

units.zh: 及明帝即位，導受遺詔輔政，解揚州，遷司徒，一依陳群輔魏故事。
units.en: When Emperor Ming succeeded, Wang Dao took the late emperor's charge as regent, surrendered the Yangzhou post for the nominal rank of minister of education—deliberately echoing Chen Qun under Wei.
units.literal: When Emperor Ming mounted the throne, Dao received the testamentary edict and assisted governance; he was relieved of Yang Province and transferred to Minister of Education, entirely following the precedent of Chen Qun assisting Wei.

units.zh: 王敦又舉兵內向。
units.en: Wang Dun rebelled again and marched on the capital.
units.literal: Wang Dun again raised troops and marched inward.

units.zh: 時敦始寢疾，導便率子弟發哀，眾聞，謂敦死，咸有奮志。
units.en: Wang Dun lay dying; Wang Dao ostentatiously went into mourning with his sons—news spread that Wang Dun was dead, and loyal troops stirred.
units.literal: At that time Dun had just fallen gravely ill; Dao then led sons and younger brothers in mourning; when the host heard, they thought Dun had died, and all had a surge of resolve.

units.zh: 及帝伐敦，假導節，都督諸軍，領揚州刺史。
units.en: When the emperor marched against Wang Dun, Wang Dao received full military credentials, overall command, and the Yangzhou inspectorate.
units.literal: When the emperor campaigned against Dun, Dao was lent a credential staff, commander of all forces, and concurrent Inspector of Yang Province.

units.zh: 敦平，進封始興郡公，邑三千戸，賜絹九千匹，進位太保，司徒如故，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名。
units.en: After the rebellion collapsed, Wang Dao became Duke of Shixing with three thousand households and nine thousand bolts of silk; he rose to grand mentor while keeping the ministry of education, with every privilege—blade at court, unhurried stride, and no need for his name at roll call.
units.literal: When Dun was pacified, Dao was advanced to Duke of Shixing commandery, three thousand households fief, nine thousand bolts of silk gifted, promoted to Grand Mentor, Minister of Education as before, sword and shoes on the palace hall, entering court without hastening, praise and obeisance without naming.

units.zh: 固讓。
units.en: He refused repeatedly.
units.literal: He firmly declined.

units.zh: 帝崩，導復與庾亮等同受遺詔，共輔幼主，是爲成帝。
units.en: When Emperor Ming died, Wang Dao and Yu Liang shared the regency for the boy who became Emperor Cheng.
units.literal: When the emperor died, Dao again together with Yu Liang and others received the testamentary edict and jointly assisted the young lord—this was Emperor Cheng.

units.zh: 加羽葆鼓吹，班劍二十人。
units.en: He received imperial pennons, drum corps, and twenty sword attendants.
units.literal: He was given feather-canopy processional music and twenty bearing swords.

units.zh: 及石勒侵阜陵，詔加導大司馬、假黃鉞，出討之。
units.en: When Shi Le struck Fuling, Wang Dao was named grand marshal with the golden axe and sent against him.
units.literal: When Shi Le invaded Fuling, an edict added Dao as Grand Marshal and lent him the yellow axe; he went out to campaign against him.

units.zh: 軍次江寧，帝親餞於郊。
units.en: The army camped at Jiangning while the young emperor saw Wang Dao off with an imperial picnic beyond the walls.
units.literal: The army halted at Jiangning; the emperor personally saw them off with a farewell feast in the suburbs.

units.zh: 俄而賊退，解大司馬。
units.en: The enemy soon withdrew, and the emergency marshal's baton was lifted.
units.literal: Soon the bandits withdrew; he was relieved of Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 庾亮將征蘇峻，訪之於導。
units.en: Yu Liang planned to attack Su Jun and asked Wang Dao's opinion.
units.literal: Yu Liang was about to campaign against Su Jun and consulted Dao.

units.zh: 導曰：「峻猜阻，必不奉詔。
units.en: Wang Dao warned, "Su Jun is suspicious and obstinate—he will not obey a summons.
units.literal: Dao said, "Jun is suspicious and obstructive; he will certainly not obey the edict.

units.zh: 且山藪藏疾，宜包容之。」
units.en: Rough country hides poisons you may have to live with—better conciliate than provoke."
units.literal: Moreover mountains and marshes harbor sickness; one ought to embrace and contain them."

units.zh: 固爭不從，亮遂召峻。
units.en: Yu Liang dismissed his advice and summoned Su Jun anyway.
units.literal: He firmly argued but was not followed; Liang thereupon summoned Jun.

units.zh: 既而難作，六軍敗績，導入宮侍帝。
units.en: Rebellion followed; imperial armies broke; Wang Dao slipped into the palace to shield the boy emperor.
units.literal: Soon thereafter disaster arose; the six armies suffered defeat; Dao entered the palace to attend the emperor.

units.zh: 峻以導德望，不敢加害，猶以本官居己之右。
units.en: Su Jun respected Wang Dao too much to harm him and left him senior in rank despite the coup.
units.literal: Because of Dao's virtue and prestige, Jun did not dare harm him; still, with his original office he placed him to his own right.

units.zh: 峻又逼乘輿幸石頭，導爭之不得。
units.en: When Su Jun dragged the court to his bastion at Stone City, Wang Dao protested in vain.
units.literal: Jun further compelled the imperial carriage to go to Stone Fort; Dao argued but could not prevail.

units.zh: 峻日來帝前肆醜言，導深懼有不測之禍。
units.en: Su Jun daily insulted the sovereign in Wang Dao's hearing; Wang Dao feared murder might follow.
units.literal: Jun daily came before the emperor and uttered vile words; Dao deeply feared there would be unforeseen disaster.

units.zh: 時路永、匡術、賈寧並説峻，令殺導，盡誅大臣，更樹腹心。
units.en: Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning urged Su Jun to kill Wang Dao, purge the ministers, and install his own creatures.
units.literal: At that time Lu Yong, Kuang Shu, and Jia Ning together urged Jun to order killing Dao, executing all great ministers wholesale, and planting new trusted intimates.

units.zh: 峻敬導，不納，故永等貳於峻。
units.en: Su Jun still respected Wang Dao and refused; Lu Yong's faction began plotting against him.
units.literal: Jun revered Dao and did not accept; therefore Yong and others became duplicitous toward Jun.

units.zh: 導使參軍袁耽潛諷誘永等，謀奉帝出奔義軍。
units.en: Wang Dao sent his aide Yuan Dan to sound out Lu Yong about spiriting the emperor to loyalist troops.
units.literal: Dao sent army adviser Yuan Dan secretly to persuade and entice Yong and others, plotting to escort the emperor out to flee to the righteous armies.

units.zh: 而峻衙禦甚嚴，事遂不果。
units.en: Su Jun's cordon was too tight and the plot collapsed.
units.literal: But Jun's defenses were very strict; the affair in the end did not succeed.

units.zh: 導乃攜二子隨永奔于白石。
units.en: Wang Dao fled with two sons alongside Lu Yong to Baishi.
units.literal: Dao then took two sons and fled with Yong to White Stone.

units.zh: 及賊平，宗廟宮室並爲灰燼，溫嶠議遷都豫章，三呉之豪請都會稽，二論紛紜，未有所適。
units.en: After the rebels fell, the palace lay in ashes; Wen Qiao urged relocating to Yuzhang while eastern elite championed Kuaiji—the debate deadlocked.
units.literal: When the bandits were pacified, ancestral temple and palace chambers alike became ashes and embers; Wen Qiao discussed moving the capital to Yuzhang; magnates of the three Wu regions requested establishing capital at Kuaiji; the two arguments clamored chaotically, and none had yet settled where to go.

units.zh: 導曰：「建康，古之金陵，舊爲帝裏，又孫仲謀、劉玄德俱言王者之宅。
units.en: Wang Dao replied, "Jiankang—ancient Jinling—was already an imperial seat; Sun Quan and Liu Bei alike called it ground fit for kings.
units.literal: Dao said, "Jiankang is ancient Jinling; formerly it was an imperial inner precinct; moreover Sun Zhongmou and Liu Xuande both pronounced it a dwelling fit for kings.

units.zh: 古之帝王不必以豐儉移都，苟弘衞文大帛之冠，則無往不可。
units.en: Ancient rulers did not necessarily move the capital because of plenty or want—if one truly practices Duke Wen of Wei's plain-silk cap, then anywhere can serve.
units.literal: The kings of old did not necessarily shift capitals because of wealth or poverty; if only one expands Duke Wen of Wei's plain silk cap, then nowhere is impossible.

units.zh: 若不績其麻，則樂土爲虛矣。
units.en: Without disciplined simplicity even the "happy land" proves hollow."
units.literal: If one does not weave its hemp, then the happy land becomes emptiness.

units.zh: 且北寇遊魂，伺我之隙，一旦示弱，竄於蠻越，求之望實，懼非良計。
units.en: Northern raiders still stalk any weakness; flee south among the tribes and you gain neither prestige nor substance—that is no strategy.
units.literal: Moreover northern bandits roam like wandering souls, watching for our gaps; once one shows weakness and flees among barbarians of Yue, seeking reputation and substance therein—I fear it is not a good plan.

units.zh: 今特宜鎮之以靜，群情自安。」
units.en: Hold steady here—stillness itself steadies the realm."
units.literal: Now it is especially fitting to stabilize them with quietness; the multitude's sentiments will of themselves be settled."

units.zh: 由是嶠等謀並不行。
units.en: The relocation faction folded.
units.literal: Thereupon Qiao's and others' plans altogether did not proceed.

units.zh: 導善於因事，雖無日用之益，而歳計有餘。
units.en: Wang Dao turned crises into advantage—little seemed gained day to day, yet the yearly accounts balanced.
units.literal: Dao was skilled at following affairs; although there was no daily-use surplus, the yearly reckoning had surplus.

units.zh: 時帑藏空竭，庫中惟有練數千端，鬻之不售，而國用不給。
units.en: State vaults were bare save thousands of bolts of fine silk nobody would buy while expenses mounted.
units.literal: At that time treasuries were empty and exhausted; in the storehouses there were only several thousand bolts of fine pale silk; selling them they would not sell, yet state expenditure was not supplied.

units.zh: 導患之，乃與朝賢俱制練布單衣，於是士人翕然競服之，練遂踴貴。
units.en: Wang Dao led courtiers in adopting plain silk robes until fashion followed—the surplus bolts suddenly fetched premium prices.
units.literal: Dao worried over it; then together with court worthies he all made plain fine-silk cloth garments; thereupon gentlemen uniformly competed to wear them, and fine silk then surged dear.

units.zh: 乃令主者出賣，端至一金。
units.en: Treasury officials sold stock at up to one gold piece per bolt.
units.literal: Then he ordered those in charge to put them out for sale; each bolt reached one gold piece.

units.zh: 其爲時所慕如此
units.en: Such was his knack for steering fashion—and solvency.
units.literal: Thus was he admired by the age.

units.zh: 六年冬，烝，詔歸胙於導，曰：「無下拜。」
units.en: In winter of the sixth year, after the great sacrifice, the emperor sent Wang Dao the ritual meat with orders: "You need not bow."
units.literal: In the sixth year, winter, the winter offering sacrifice; an edict returned the sacrificial meat to Dao, saying, "Do not descend to bow."

units.zh: 導辭疾不敢當。
units.en: Wang Dao pleaded ill and refused the privilege.
units.literal: Dao declined on grounds of illness and did not dare accept.

units.zh: 初，帝幼沖，見導，每拜。
units.en: While still a child, Emperor Cheng had bowed each time he met Wang Dao.
units.literal: At first, when the emperor was young and tender, whenever he saw Dao, each time he bowed.

units.zh: 又嘗與導書手詔，則云「惶恐言」，中書作詔，則曰「敬問」，於是以爲定制。
units.en: His autograph letters began "I speak with trepidation"; palace drafts addressed Wang Dao with "respectful inquiry"—those formulae became precedent.
units.literal: Moreover he once wrote Dao in his own hand an edict that said "speaking with trepidation"; when the Palace Writers drafted edicts, they said "respectfully inquire"; thereby this became fixed regulation.

units.zh: 自後元正，導入，帝猶爲之興焉。
units.en: Even at New Year's audiences the young emperor rose when Wang Dao appeared.
units.literal: Afterward at New Year's Day, when Dao entered, the emperor still rose for him.

units.zh: 時大旱，導上疏遜位。
units.en: During a severe drought Wang Dao offered to resign.
units.literal: At that time there was great drought; Dao submitted a memorial yielding his position.

units.zh: 詔曰：「夫聖王禦世，動合至道，運無不周，故能人倫攸敘，萬物獲宜。
units.en: The throne replied: "A sage king moves with the Way, leaves nothing uncovered, sets human relations right, and lets creation thrive.
units.literal: An edict said, "As for the sage king governing the age, his movements accord with the utmost Way; his circuit lacks nothing not pervaded; therefore human relationships are thereby ordered and the myriad things obtain fitness.

units.zh: 朕荷祖宗之重，托于王公之上，不能仰陶玄風，俯洽宇宙，亢陽逾時，兆庶胥怨，邦之不臧，惟予一人。
units.en: We inherit a heavy charge yet cannot spread moral influence or harmonize heaven and earth—prolonged drought and popular anger are our fault alone.
units.literal: We bear the weight of ancestors and fathers, entrusted above ducal lords and kings; unable to upward mold ourselves to the dark wind, downward harmonize the cosmos—overlong drought, omen multitudes all resent; the state's ill fortune lies only in Us alone.

units.zh: 公體道明哲，弘猶深遠，勳格四海，翼亮三世，國典之不墜，實仲山甫補之。
units.en: You embody clarity of principle, your merit spans the seas, you have steadied three reigns—without you our institutions would long ago have collapsed, as surely as Zhong Shanfu upheld the Zhou.
units.literal: The Duke embodies the Way, enlightened and wise; his breadth is deep and far-reaching; his merit reaches the four seas; he has wing-brightened three reigns; that the state's canons have not fallen is truly because Zhong Shanfu mends them.

units.zh: 而猥崇謙光，引咎克讓，元道之愆，寄責宰輔，只增其闕。
units.en: Yet you insist on humble gestures and shoulder blame that belongs on our throne—such misplaced virtue only widens the fault.
units.literal: Yet basely you elevate humble radiance, drawing blame and yielding—the primal Way's fault, lodging blame on chief ministers—only increases its deficiencies.

units.zh: 博綜萬機，不可一日有曠。
units.en: The myriad affairs cannot sit idle even for a day.
units.literal: Broadly overseeing the myriad pivots—there cannot be one day of vacancy.

units.zh: 公宜遺履謙之近節，遵經國之遠略。
units.en: Abandon excessive modesty and keep your eye on the long governance of the realm.
units.literal: The Duke ought to cast away nearby restraint of treading humility and follow the far-ranging strategy of ordering the state.

units.zh: 門下速遣侍中以下敦喻。」
units.en: Have the Gate Bureau send attendants at once to urge you back to duty."
units.literal: Let the Gate Bureau swiftly dispatch Palace Attendants downward earnestly to instruct."

units.zh: 導固讓。
units.en: Wang Dao still refused.
units.literal: Dao firmly declined.

units.zh: 詔累逼之，然後視事。
units.en: Repeated edicts pressed him until he returned to office.
units.literal: Edicts repeatedly pressed him; only afterward did he attend to affairs.

units.zh: 導簡素寡欲，倉無儲穀，衣不重帛。
units.en: Wang Dao lived plainly—empty bins at home and never layered silk.
units.literal: Dao was plain and simple and had few desires; his granaries stored no grain; his garments did not double-layer silk.

units.zh: 帝知之，給布萬匹，以供私費。
units.en: Learning this, the emperor granted ten thousand bolts for household needs.
units.literal: The emperor knew it and supplied ten thousand bolts of cloth to supply private expenses.

units.zh: 導有羸疾，不堪朝會，帝幸其府，縱酒作樂，後令輿車入殿，其見敬如此。
units.en: Ill health kept Wang Dao from court, so the emperor held revels in his mansion and later allowed his carriage into the palace arcade—such was the esteem he commanded.
units.literal: Dao had wasting illness and could not endure court assemblies; the emperor visited his residence, indulged wine and made music; afterward he ordered litter-carriages to enter the palace halls—thus was he respected.

units.zh: 石季龍掠騎至曆陽，導請出討之。
units.en: When Shi Hu's horsemen pushed as far as Liyang, Wang Dao volunteered to lead the response.
units.literal: Shi Jilong's raiding horsemen reached Liyang; Dao requested to go out and campaign against them.

units.zh: 加大司馬、假黃鉞、中外諸軍事，置左右長史、司馬，給布萬匹。
units.en: He received the grand marshal's title, the yellow axe, full military command, a full staff, and ten thousand bolts of cloth.
units.literal: He was added Grand Marshal, lent yellow axe, command of military affairs within and without; left and right senior clerks and majors were established; ten thousand bolts of cloth supplied.

units.zh: 俄而賊退，解大司馬，復轉中外大都督，進位太傅，又拜丞相，依漢制罷司徒官以並之。
units.en: The raiders soon withdrew; Wang Dao shed the emergency marshal's role, took overall command, became grand tutor, and was named chancellor—civil and military authority merged, the minister of education post retired per Han precedent.
units.literal: Soon the bandits withdrew; he was relieved of Grand Marshal, again transferred to grand commander of all within and without, advanced to Grand Tutor, also appointed Chancellor, and following Han system the Minister of Education post was abolished to merge with it.

units.zh: 冊曰：「朕夙罹不造，肆陟帝位，未堪多難，禍亂旁興。
units.en: The investiture read: "We came early to the throne in hard times, ill prepared for one crisis after another.
units.literal: The investiture document said, "We from youth have met ill fate, therefore ascended the imperial seat, not able to bear many calamities; disaster and disorder arise on every side.

units.zh: 公文貫九功，武經七德，外緝四海，內齊八政，天地以平，人神以和，業同伊尹，道隆姬旦。
units.en: In civil policy you thread the nine tasks; in arms the seven virtues; you bind the four seas without and order the eight ministries within—Heaven and earth settle, gods and men accord—your service rivals Yi Yin, your stature matches the Duke of Zhou.
units.literal: The Duke's pattern threads the nine achievements; in military he threads the seven virtues; without he gathers the four seas; within he aligns the eight policies; Heaven and Earth thereby are leveled, men and spirits thereby harmonized; his enterprise matches Yi Yin, his Way is exalted like Ji Dan.

units.zh: 仰思唐虞，登庸雋乂，申命群官，允釐庶績。
units.en: As Tang and Yu elevated worthy ministers and charged each office to clarify its duties—
units.literal: Looking up we ponder Tang and Yu, promoting employment of outstanding talent; repeatedly commanding hosts of officials, truly regulating the manifold accomplishments.

units.zh: 朕思憑高謨，弘濟遠獻，維稽古建爾於上公，永爲晉輔。
units.en: —we therefore appoint you supreme duke by ancient precedent, Jin's pillar hereafter.
units.literal: We think to rely on lofty stratagems, broadly succoring far-reaching presentations; by examining antiquity We establish you as supreme duke, forever to be Jin's assistant.

units.zh: 往踐厥職，敬敷道訓，以亮天工。
units.en: Take up your charge, spread moral instruction, and give bright aid to Heaven's work.
units.literal: Go tread those duties; respectfully spread the teaching of the Way, thereby to brighten Heaven's work.

units.zh: 不亦休哉！
units.en: What greater blessing could there be?
units.literal: Is it not splendid!

units.zh: 公其戒之！」
units.en: Bear these words in mind!"
units.literal: Duke, guard yourself in this!"

units.zh: 是歳，妻曹氏卒，贈金章紫綬。
units.en: That year Lady Cao died; she was posthumously honored with a gold seal and purple ribbon.
units.literal: That year his wife Lady Cao died; she was gifted golden seal and purple ribbon.

units.zh: 初，曹氏性妒，導甚憚之，乃密營別館，以處眾妾。
units.en: Lady Cao was fiercely jealous, so Wang Dao quietly kept a second house for his concubines.
units.literal: At first Lady Cao's nature was jealous; Dao greatly feared her; then he secretly built a separate lodge to house his host of concubines.

units.zh: 曹氏知，將往焉。
units.en: When she learned of it, she stormed toward the house.
units.literal: When Lady Cao learned, she was about to go there.

units.zh: 導恐妾被辱，遽令命駕，猶恐遲之，以所執麈尾柄驅牛而進。
units.en: Fearing for his concubines, Wang Dao ordered his carriage at once and even beat the ox with his yak-tail fan's handle to gain speed.
units.literal: Dao feared the concubines would suffer insult; he hurriedly ordered his carriage harnessed, still fearing delay; with the yak-tail handle he grasped he drove the ox forward.

units.zh: 司徒蔡謨聞之，戲導曰：「朝廷欲加公九錫。」
units.en: Minister Cai Mo quipped, "The court means to award you the Nine Insignia."
units.literal: Minister of Education Cai Mo heard it and playfully said to Dao, "The court wishes to add to the Duke the Nine Bestowals."

units.zh: 導弗之覺，但謙退而已。
units.en: Wang Dao missed the joke and demurred politely.
units.literal: Dao did not perceive it; he only modestly demurred.

units.zh: 謨曰：「不聞餘物，惟有短轅犢車，長柄麈尾。」
units.en: Cai Mo added, "Nothing costly—only a calf cart with a stub axle and that long-handled yak-tail fan."
units.literal: Mo said, "I have not heard of other objects—only a short-axle calf cart and a long-handled yak-tail."

units.zh: 導大怒，謂人曰：「吾往與群賢共遊洛中，何曾聞有蔡克兒也。」
units.en: Wang Dao flushed with rage. "When we walked Luoyang among the worthy," he snapped, "who had heard of Cai Ke's boy?"
units.literal: Dao was greatly angry and said to others, "When I formerly roamed Luoyang together with hosts of worthies, how ever did I hear of Cai Ke's son!"

units.zh: 于時庾亮以望重地逼，出鎮於外。
units.en: Yu Liang's prestige had begun to grate—he was posted to a frontier command.
units.literal: At that time Yu Liang, because his prestige was weighty and his base pressing, went out to command outside.

units.zh: 南蠻校尉陶稱間説亮當舉兵內向，或勸導密爲之防。
units.en: Colonel Tao Cheng whispered that Yu Liang planned to march on the capital; some urged Wang Dao to prepare in secret.
units.literal: Southern Barbarians Colonel Tao Cheng secretly spread word that Liang was about to raise troops and march inward; some urged Dao secretly to guard against it.

units.zh: 導曰：「吾與元規休戚是同，悠悠之談，宜絶智者之口。
units.en: Wang Dao replied, "Yu Liang and I rise or fall together—wise men should silence idle rumor.
units.literal: Dao said, "Yuangui and I share joy and sorrow alike; idle chatter ought to be cut off from the mouths of the wise.

units.zh: 則如君言，元規若來，吾便角巾還第，復何懼哉！」
units.en: If he truly came, I would tie my kerchief like a private gentleman and go home—why should I fear?"
units.literal: Then as my lord says—if Yuangui comes, I shall simply don scholar's kerchief and return to my mansion—what again is there to fear!"

units.zh: 又與稱書，以爲庾公帝之元舅，宜善事之。
units.en: He wrote Tao Cheng again: Yu Liang was the emperor's senior uncle—treat him with respect.
units.literal: He also wrote Cheng a letter, holding that Duke Yu was the emperor's eldest maternal uncle and ought to be served well.

units.zh: 於是讒間遂息。
units.en: The whispering campaign died away.
units.literal: Thereupon slander and estrangement ceased.

units.zh: 時亮雖居外鎮，而執朝廷之權，既據上流，擁強兵，趣向者多歸之。
units.en: Yu Liang stayed upriver yet pulled court strings—powerful gentry flocked to him.
units.literal: At that time although Liang dwelt in an outer command, he grasped court power; having occupied the upper reaches and possessing strong troops, those whose inclinations followed mostly attached to him.

units.zh: 導內不能平，常遇西風塵起，舉扇自蔽，徐曰：「元規塵汙人。」
units.en: Privately Wang Dao seethed—whenever dust blew from the west he raised his fan and murmured, "That man's grit dirties everyone."
units.literal: Dao inwardly could not be at peace; whenever he met west wind and dust rising, he raised a fan to shield himself and slowly said, "Yuangui's dust soils people."

units.zh: 自漢魏以來，群臣不拜山陵。
units.en: Since Han and Wei times ministers had not bowed at imperial tombs.
units.literal: From Han and Wei onward, hosts of ministers did not bow at imperial tombs.

units.zh: 導以元帝睠同布衣，匪惟君臣而已，每一崇進，皆就拜，不勝哀戚。
units.en: Wang Dao had shared Emperor Yuan's friendship as a commoner—not merely as lord and subject—so each time he approached the tomb he bowed, overcome with grief.
units.literal: Because Dao regarded Emperor Yuan's affection as like plain cloth—it was not only lord and minister—each time there was elevation and advancement, he all went and bowed, unable to bear grief.

units.zh: 由是詔百官拜陵，自導始也。
units.en: Henceforth officials bowed at imperial tombs—a precedent Wang Dao began.
units.literal: Thereby an edict commanded the hundred offices to bow at tombs; it began with Dao.

units.zh: 咸康五年薨，時年六十四。
units.en: In the fifth year of Xiankang, he died at sixty-four.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Xiankang, he died; at the time age sixty-four.

units.zh: 帝舉哀於朝堂三日，遣大鴻臚持節監護喪事，賵襚之禮，一依漢博陸侯及安平獻王故事。
units.en: The court mourned three days in session; the Grand Herald oversaw the funeral with Han-era honors matching Huo Guang and the Prince of Anping.
units.literal: The emperor expressed grief in the court hall three days; he dispatched the Grand Herald bearing staff to supervise and guard funeral affairs; gifts for burial followed ritual entirely according to Han Baron of Bolu and Prince Xian of Anping precedents.

units.zh: 及葬，給九游轀輬車、黃屋左纛、前後羽葆鼓吹、武賁班劍百人，中興名臣莫與爲比。
units.en: His procession included the nine-banner hearse, imperial yellow canopy, guards of honor front and rear—no minister of the restored dynasty matched such pageantry.
units.literal: When he was buried, there were supplied nine-pennon hearse wagon, yellow canopy left banner, front and rear feather-canopy processional music, one hundred martial guards bearing swords—among restored Jin's famed ministers none compared.

units.zh: 冊曰：「蓋高位以酬明德，厚爵以答懋勳；
units.en: The posthumous patent read: "High office honors luminous virtue; noble titles repay towering merit;
units.literal: The investiture document said, "In general high position rewards bright virtue; generous noble rank answers splendid merit;

units.zh: 至乎闔棺標跡，莫尚號諡，風流百代，於是乎在。
units.en: when the lid closes, nothing surpasses a fitting posthumous name—his influence will ride down the ages.
units.literal: As for closing the coffin and marking traces, nothing is greater than title and posthumous name; refinement flowing through hundred generations lies herein.

units.zh: 惟公邁達沖虛，玄鑒劭邈；
units.en: You moved through the world with transparent humility and vision few could match;
units.literal: Only the Duke strides transcendent and empty-vast; dark mirror splendid and remote;

units.zh: 夷淡以約其心，體仁以流其惠；
units.en: simplicity stilled your heart while humanity spread your kindness;
units.literal: plain blandness to restrain his heart, embodying benevolence to spread his kindness;

units.zh: 棲遲務外，則名雋中夏，應期濯纓，則潛算獨運。
units.en: in retirement your fame filled the central lands; when summoned you cleared office like one rinsing his cap—yet strategy ran quietly through your hands.
units.literal: dwelling leisurely attending outward affairs, then fame was eminent within the central Xia; responding to season washing cap tassels, then hidden reckoning alone operated.

units.zh: 昔我中宗、肅祖之基中興也，下帷委誠而策定江左，拱己宅心而庶績咸熙。
units.en: When Zhongzong and Suzu rebuilt the dynasty, you plotted behind curtains to anchor the southeast and folded your hands in trust until every office flourished.
units.literal: Formerly when our Zhongzong and Suzu founded the restoration, lowering curtains entrusting sincerity, stratagems settled the left bank of the Yangzi; folding hands dwelling in heart, then manifold accomplishments all shone.

units.zh: 故能威之所振，寇虐改心，化之所鼓，檮杌易質；
units.en: Where your majesty reached, enemies relented; where your influence spread, savages changed their nature;
units.literal: Therefore where awe extended, bandits and tyrants changed hearts; where transformation drummed, taowu changed substance;

units.zh: 調陰陽之和，通彝倫之紀，遼隴承風，丹穴景附。
units.en: yin and yang aligned, human ties held—even distant Long submitted and southern tribes clustered close.
units.literal: harmonizing yin and yang's accord, penetrating constant human relationships' warp; distant Long obeyed the wind, cinnabar grotto drew near in attachment.

units.zh: 隆高世之功，復宣武之績，舊物不失，公協其猷。
units.en: You magnified age-spanning deeds and restored imperial fortunes—nothing was lost while you shaped policy.
units.literal: Raising high-generation merit, restoring Xuanyu's accomplishment; old things not lost—the Duke harmonized those plans.

units.zh: 若乃荷負顧命，保朕沖人，遭遇艱圮，夷險委順；
units.en: You bore dying charge to shield Us as a child—through collapse you smoothed every peril.
units.literal: As for bearing testamentary charge, protecting Us tender child, encountering hardship and ruin, leveling peril and entrusting compliance;

units.zh: 拯其淪墜而濟之以道，扶其頹傾而弘之以仁，經緯三朝而蘊道彌曠。
units.en: You rescued the drowning with principle, steadied the falling with humanity, and threaded three reigns while your stores of wisdom seemed inexhaustible.
units.literal: rescuing those sinking and drowning and ferrying them with the Way; supporting those toppling and leaning and enlarging them with benevolence; weaving warp and weft through three reigns while harboring the Way ever more vast.

units.zh: 方賴高謨，以穆四海，昊天不吊，奄忽薨殂，朕用震慟於心。
units.en: We still leaned on your counsel to pacify the realm—yet Heaven showed no mercy and claimed you suddenly; Our heart jars with grief.
units.literal: Just when relying on lofty stratagem to harmonize the four seas, August Heaven did not pity—suddenly he died; We therefore quake with grief in heart.

units.zh: 雖有殷之殞保衡，有周之喪二南，曷諭茲懷！
units.en: Shang mourned its Yi Yin; Zhou mourned the southern odes—what compares to Our sorrow?
units.literal: Although Yin lost its Protecting Marshall, Zhou mourned the two southern collections—how express this feeling!

units.zh: 今遣使持節、謁者僕射任瞻錫諡曰文獻，祠乙太牢。
units.en: We send Herald Vice Director Ren Zhan to confer the posthumous title Literature and Presentation and offer the grand sacrifice.
units.literal: Now We dispatch Credential Bearer, Herald Vice Director Ren Zhan to grant posthumous title Wenxian, sacrificing with grand beast offering at the temple.

units.zh: 魂而有靈，嘉茲榮寵！」
units.en: If any consciousness remains, delight in this honor!"
units.literal: If soul has spirit, rejoice in this glorious favor!"

units.zh: 二弟：穎、敞，少與導俱知名，時人以穎方溫太真，以敞比鄧伯道，並早卒。
units.en: His brothers Wang Ying and Wang Chang were celebrated with him—likened to Wen Jiao and Deng You—but both died young.
units.literal: Two younger brothers: Ying and Chang—in youth together with Dao were both renowned; men of the time compared Ying to Wen Taizhen, compared Chang to Deng Bodao; both died early.

units.zh: 導六子：悅、恬、洽、協、邵、薈。
units.en: Wang Dao fathered six sons: Yue, Tian, Qia, Xie, Shao, and Hui.
units.literal: Dao had six sons: Yue, Tian, Qia, Xie, Shao, and Hui.

units.zh: 導子 悅
units.en: Wang Yue, son of Wang Dao
units.literal: Dao's son Yue.

units.zh: 悅字長豫，弱冠有高名，事親色養，導甚愛之。
units.en: Wang Yue, courtesy Changyu, won fame young and cared for his parents with devotion—Wang Dao adored him.
units.literal: Yue, courtesy name Changyu, at weak crown had high renown; serving parents he nurtured by cheerful demeanor; Dao greatly loved him.

units.zh: 導嘗共悅奕棋，爭道，導笑曰：「相與有瓜葛，那得爲爾邪！」
units.en: Once they quarreled over a chess move; Wang Dao laughed and said, "We are family—why scrape over stones?"
units.literal: Dao once played weiqi with Yue and disputed a move; Dao smiled and said, "Mutually we have melon-vine connections—how can we act thus to each other!"

units.zh: 導性儉節，帳下甘果爛敗，令棄之，云：「勿使大郎知。」
units.en: Though Wang Dao lived frugally, when fruit spoiled under his tent he told servants to discard it quietly—"Don't let the eldest boy hear."
units.literal: Dao's nature was frugal; sweet fruits under his tent rotted; he ordered them discarded, saying, "Do not let the elder young lord know."

units.zh: 悅少侍講東宮，歷呉王友、中書侍郎，先導卒，諡貞世子。
units.en: He lectured in the heir's palace, served as companion to the Prince of Wu and gentleman of the palace writers, and predeceased his father with the posthumous epithet Steadfast Heir.
units.literal: Yue in youth lectured in attendance at the Eastern Palace; he passed through Friend to the Prince of Wu and Gentleman of the Palace Writers; he died before Dao; posthumous title Heir Who Is Steadfast.

units.zh: 先是，導夢人以百萬錢買悅，潛爲祈禱者備矣。
units.en: Earlier Wang Dao dreamed someone bought his son for a million cash and quietly funded prayers on his behalf.
units.literal: Before this, Dao dreamed a man bought Yue for a million cash; secretly he prepared prayers for those who prayed.

units.zh: 尋掘地，得錢百萬，意甚惡之，一皆藏閉。
units.en: Soon afterward laborers unearthed exactly that sum—Wang Dao took it as an evil omen and locked every coin away.
units.literal: Soon digging earth, they obtained a million cash; his intention was very ill-omened; he altogether stored and sealed them.

units.zh: 及悅疾篤，導憂念特至，不食積日。
units.en: When Wang Yue sank toward death, Wang Dao grew frantic and refused food for days.
units.literal: When Yue's illness was grave, Dao's anxious thoughts were extreme; he did not eat for accumulated days.

units.zh: 忽見一人形狀甚偉，被甲持刀，導問：「君是何人？」
units.en: Suddenly an armored giant with a saber appeared; Wang Dao demanded, "Who are you?"
units.literal: Suddenly he saw a man whose form was very imposing, clad in armor holding a blade; Dao asked, "Who are you, sir?"

units.zh: 曰：「僕是蔣侯也。
units.en: I am the River Earl Jiang," came the reply.
units.literal: He said, "Your servant is Lord Jiang.

units.zh: 公兒不佳，欲爲請命，故來耳。
units.en: Your son fails—I've come to plead for him with Heaven.
units.literal: Your lordship's son is not well; I wish to seek life for him—therefore I have come.

units.zh: 公勿復憂。」
units.en: Do not despair."
units.literal: Your lordship need not further worry."

units.zh: 因求食，遂啖數升。
units.en: He asked for food and devoured several pints.
units.literal: Thereupon he sought food; then he ate several sheng.

units.zh: 食畢，勃然謂導曰：「中書患，非可救者。」
units.en: When he finished he turned grim: "The Palace Writer's affliction is not one that can be saved."
units.literal: When eating finished, abruptly he said to Dao, "The Zhongshu affliction—none who may save it."

units.zh: 言訖不見，悅亦殞絶。
units.en: He vanished; Wang Yue died at once.
units.literal: When words ended he was not seen; Yue also expired.

units.zh: 悅與導語，恆以慎密爲端。
units.en: In conversation Wang Yue always urged discretion.
units.literal: When Yue spoke with Dao, he always took cautious secrecy as the beginning.

units.zh: 導還台，及行，悅未嘗不送至車後，又恆爲母曹氏襞斂箱篋中物。
units.en: Whenever Wang Dao left for court, Wang Yue walked him to his carriage and quietly packed Lady Cao's traveling chests.
units.literal: When Dao returned to the terrace, whenever he traveled, Yue never failed to escort to behind the carriage; moreover he always for mother Lady Cao folded and gathered objects in chests and boxes.

units.zh: 悅亡後，導還台，自悅常所送處哭至台門，其母長封作篋，不忍復開。
units.en: After Wang Yue died Wang Dao wept from the spot where they had parted all the way to the palace gate; Lady Cao sealed her son's chests forever.
units.literal: After Yue died, when Dao returned to the terrace, from the place Yue always escorted he wept to the terrace gate; his mother long sealed and made a chest, unable to bear opening again.

units.zh: 悅無子，以弟恬子琨爲嗣，襲導爵丹陽尹，卒，贈太常。
units.en: Childless, Wang Yue adopted his nephew Wang Kun, who inherited titles and served as governor of Danyang; he died honored as minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: Yue had no sons; he took younger brother Tian's son Kun as heir; Kun inherited Dao's noble rank and was Governor of Danyang; when he died, he was gifted Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 子嘏嗣，尚鄱陽公主，歷中領軍、尚書。
units.en: His son Wang Jia succeeded him, married the Princess of Poyang, and rose to central army commander and minister.
units.literal: His son Jia succeeded; he married Princess Poyang; he passed through Central Army Commander and Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 卒，子恢嗣，義熙末，爲遊擊將軍。
units.en: He was succeeded by Wang Hui, who at the end of the Yixi era was a mobile corps general.
units.literal: When he died, his son Hui succeeded; at the end of the Yixi era, he was Mobile Corps General.

units.zh: 悅弟 恬
units.en: Wang Tian, younger brother of Wang Yue
units.literal: Yue's younger brother Tian.

units.zh: 恬字敬豫。
units.en: His courtesy name was Jingyu.
units.literal: Tian, courtesy name Jingyu.

units.zh: 少好武，不爲公門所重。
units.en: He loved soldierly pursuits and earned little credit among grandees.
units.literal: In youth he loved martial affairs; he was not esteemed by ducal gates.

units.zh: 導見悅輒喜，見恬便有怒色。
units.en: Wang Dao lit up at sight of Wang Yue but scowled whenever Wang Tian appeared.
units.literal: Whenever Dao saw Yue he was glad; whenever he saw Tian there was angry color.

units.zh: 州辟別駕，不行，襲爵即丘子。
units.en: He declined a provincial aide post and inherited the barony of Jiqiu.
units.literal: The province summoned him as Attendant Clerk; he did not go; he inherited noble rank as Baron of Jiqiu.

units.zh: 性傲誕，不拘禮法。
units.en: He was arrogant and flouted etiquette.
units.literal: His nature was arrogant and extravagant; he did not bind himself to ritual law.

units.zh: 謝萬嘗造恬，既坐，少頃，恬便入內。
units.en: Once Xie Wan called on him; shortly after they sat, Wang Tian vanished indoors.
units.literal: Xie Wan once visited Tian; after seating, in a little while Tian then entered within.

units.zh: 萬以爲必厚待己，殊有喜色。
units.en: Xie Wan assumed a lavish reception awaited and looked delighted.
units.literal: Wan thought he must be generously treating himself and had especially pleased expression.

units.zh: 恬久之乃沐頭散發而出，據胡床於庭中曬發，神氣傲邁，竟無賓主之禮。
units.en: Wang Tian eventually reappeared with wet hair loose, lounged on a camp stool in the courtyard drying it—utterly ignoring guest ritual.
units.literal: After long Tian then washed his head and scattered hair and came out; he leaned on a folding stool in the courtyard drying hair; spirit bearing arrogant and lofty—utterly lacking guest-host ritual.

units.zh: 萬悵然而歸。
units.en: Xie Wan left in dismay.
units.literal: Wan returned disappointed.

units.zh: 晩節更好士，多技藝，善奕棋，爲中興第一。
units.en: Late in life he cultivated talent, mastered many arts, and ranked first among weiqi players of the restored court.
units.literal: In late years he further valued gentlemen; he had many skills and arts; he was skilled at weiqi—first under the restoration.

units.zh: 遷中書郎。
units.en: He rose to gentleman of the palace writers.
units.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Writers.

units.zh: 帝欲以爲中書令，導固讓，從之。
units.en: The emperor wanted him as director of the palace writers; Wang Dao refused on his behalf and the appointment lapsed.
units.literal: The emperor wished to make him Director of the Palace Writers; Dao firmly declined; they followed him.

units.zh: 除後將軍、魏郡太守，加給事中，領兵鎮石頭。
units.en: He took general of the rear, prefect of Wei, attendant within, and commanded the garrison at Stone City.
units.literal: He was appointed General of the Rear, Prefect of Wei commandery, added Attendant Within, commanding troops garrisoning Stone Fort.

units.zh: 導薨，去官。
units.en: He resigned when Wang Dao died.
units.literal: When Dao died, he left office.

units.zh: 俄起爲後將軍，復鎮石頭。
units.en: Soon he returned as general of the rear at Stone City.
units.literal: Soon he was raised as General of the Rear, again garrisoning Stone Fort.

units.zh: 轉呉國、會稽內史，加散騎常侍。
units.en: He governed Wu and Kuaiji as interior clerk and picked up cavalier attendant.
units.literal: He was transferred to Interior Clerk of Wu and Kuaiji, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
