units.zh: 卒，贈中軍將軍，諡曰憲。
units.en: He died honored as general of the central army with the posthumous epithet Disciplined.
units.literal: When he died, he was gifted General of the Central Army; posthumous title was Xian.

units.zh: 恬弟 洽
units.en: Wang Qia, younger brother of Wang Tian
units.literal: Tian's younger brother Qia.

units.zh: 洽字敬和，導諸子中最知名，與荀羨俱有美稱。
units.en: Wang Qia, courtesy Jinghe, was the best known of Wang Dao's sons and shared Xun Xian's glowing reputation.
units.literal: Qia, courtesy name Jinghe, among Dao's sons was most renowned; together with Xun Xian both had fine reputations.

units.zh: 弱冠，歷散騎、中書郎、中軍長史、司徒左長史、建武將軍、呉郡內史。
units.en: While still young he rose through cavalier attendant, palace writer, central army and ministry clerkships, general who establishes might, and Wu interior clerk.
units.literal: At weak crown he passed through Cavalier Attendant, Gentleman of the Palace Writers, Senior Clerk of the Central Army, Senior Clerk of the Minister of Education's Left, General Who Establishes Might, Interior Clerk of Wu commandery.

units.zh: 徵拜領軍，尋加中書令，固讓，表疏十上。
units.en: Summoned as commander of the guards and soon offered the palace directorate, he declined ten memorials running.
units.literal: He was summoned and appointed Army Commander; soon added Director of the Palace Writers; he firmly declined; memorials and petitions ten times submitted.

units.zh: 穆帝詔曰：「敬和清裁貴令，昔爲中書郎，吾時尚小，數呼見，意甚親之。
units.en: Emperor Mu wrote: "Wang Qia's judgment is lucid and noble. When he served as palace writer I was still a boy yet loved to summon him—we were close.
units.literal: Emperor Mu's edict said, "Jinghe's pure judgment is noble and admirable; formerly when he was Gentleman of the Palace Writers, We were still small; repeatedly We summoned him to audience; Our intention greatly cherished him.

units.zh: 今所以用爲令，既機任須才，且欲時時相見，共講文章，待以友臣之義。
units.en: We name him director because the post demands genius—and because We long to study literature with him as friend as well as minister.
units.literal: Now the reason for employing him as Director is both that pivotal duty requires talent, and also We wish constantly to see each other, together discussing literary compositions, treating him with the righteousness of friend-minister.

units.zh: 而累表固讓，甚違本懷。
units.en: Persistent refusal cuts against Our wishes.
units.literal: Yet repeatedly memorializing firm yielding—greatly violates Our original intent.

units.zh: 其催洽令拜。」
units.en: See that he accepts at once."
units.literal: Urge Qia to command him to bow acceptance."

units.zh: 苦讓，遂不受。
units.en: He still refused every summons.
units.literal: He bitterly yielded; in the end he did not accept.

units.zh: 昇平二年卒於官，年三十六。
units.en: In the second year of Shengping, he died in office at thirty-six.
units.literal: In the second year of Shengping, he died in office, age thirty-six.

units.zh: 二子：珣、瑉。
units.en: His sons were Wang Xun and Wang Min.
units.literal: Two sons: Xun and Min.

units.zh: 洽子 珣
units.en: Wang Xun, son of Wang Qia
units.literal: Qia's son Xun.

units.zh: 珣字元琳。
units.en: His courtesy name was Yuanlin.
units.literal: Xun, courtesy name Yuanlin.

units.zh: 弱冠與陳郡謝玄爲桓溫掾，俱爲溫所敬重，嘗謂之曰：「謝掾年四十，必擁旄杖節。
units.en: While still young he and Xie Xuan served Huan Wen as clerks—both were favorites. Huan Wen once said, "When Clerk Xie reaches forty he will command a province.
units.literal: At weak crown together with Xie Xuan of Chen commandery he was Huan Wen's clerk; both were revered by Wen; Wen once said to them, "Clerk Xie at age forty will surely wield banner and staff credential.

units.zh: 王掾當作黑頭公。
units.en: Clerk Wang will wear black hair into the minister's seat.
units.literal: Clerk Wang ought to become black-headed duke.

units.zh: 皆未易才也。」
units.en: Neither talent will easily be matched."
units.literal: Both are talents not easily matched."

units.zh: 珣轉主簿。
units.en: Wang Xun became chief clerk.
units.literal: Xun was transferred to chief clerk.

units.zh: 時溫經略中夏，竟無寧歳，軍中機務並委珣焉。
units.en: Huan Wen campaigned endlessly in the north and entrusted every military secret to Wang Xun.
units.literal: At that time Wen planned strategy in central Xia; ultimately there was no peaceful year; army affairs of pivotal duties were all entrusted to Xun.

units.zh: 文武數萬人，悉識其面。
units.en: He knew every face among tens of thousands of officers and men.
units.literal: Civil and martial several tens of thousands—all knew his face.

units.zh: 從討袁真，封東亭侯，轉大司馬參軍、琅邪王友、中軍長史、給事黃門侍郎。
units.en: He joined the campaign against Yuan Zhen, became Marquis of East Pavilion, then adjutant to the grand marshal, tutor to the Prince of Langye, central army clerk, and yellow-gates attendant.
units.literal: He followed in campaigning against Yuan Zhen; was enfeoffed Marquis of East Pavilion; transferred to Army Adjutant of Grand Marshal, Friend to the Prince of Langye, Senior Clerk of Central Army, Serving Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.

units.zh: 珣兄弟皆謝氏婿，以猜嫌致隙。
units.en: Both Wang brothers married Xie women; jealousy split the families.
units.literal: Xun and his younger brother were both sons-in-law of the Xie clan; because of suspicion and mistrust they caused rifts.

units.zh: 太傅安既與珣絶婚，又離瑉妻，由是二族遂成仇釁。
units.en: Grand Tutor Xie An annulled Wang Xun's marriage and drove Wang Min's wife away—the two houses became bitter foes.
units.literal: Grand Tutor An having already severed marriage with Xun, further divorced Min's wife; thereby the two clans then became hostile grievance.

units.zh: 時希安旨，乃出珣爲豫章太守，不之官。
units.en: Trying to placate Xie An, the court named Wang Xun prefect of Yuzhang—he never took up the post.
units.literal: At the time hoping for An's intent, then Xun was sent out as Prefect of Yuzhang; he did not go to office.

units.zh: 除散騎常侍，不拜。
units.en: He declined appointment as cavalier attendant.
units.literal: He was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary; he did not accept.

units.zh: 遷秘書監。
units.en: He rose to supervisor of the palace library.
units.literal: He was transferred to Supervisor of the Palace Library.

units.zh: 安卒後，遷侍中，孝武深杖之。
units.en: After Xie An died he became palace attendant—Emperor Xiaowu leaned on him heavily.
units.literal: After An died, he was transferred to Palace Attendant; Emperor Xiaowu deeply relied on him.

units.zh: 轉輔國將軍、呉國內史，在郡爲士庶所悅。
units.en: As general who supports the state and Wu interior clerk he won gentry and commoners alike.
units.literal: He was transferred to General Who Supports the State and Interior Clerk of Wu; in the commandery he was pleasing to gentry and commoners.

units.zh: 徵爲尚書右僕射，領吏部，轉左僕射，加征虜將軍，復領太子詹事。
units.en: He was called to vice director of the Masters of Writing, personnel chief, then left vice director with general who subdues brigands and superintendent of the heir's household.
units.literal: He was summoned as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Right, concurrent Personnel Ministry; transferred to Vice Director Left, added General Who Subdues Brigands, again concurrent Household Superintendent for the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 時帝雅好典籍，珣與殷仲堪、徐邈、王恭、郗恢等並以才學文章見昵於帝。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowu loved books; Wang Xun joined Yin Zhongkan, Xu Miao, Wang Gong, and Xi Hui as scholarly favorites at court.
units.literal: At that time the emperor greatly loved canonical texts; Xun together with Yin Zhongkan, Xu Miao, Wang Gong, Xi Hui and others all by talent learning and literary compositions were viewed intimately by the emperor.

units.zh: 及王國寶自媚于會稽王道子，而與珣等不協，帝慮晏駕後怨隙必生，故出恭、恢爲方伯，而委珣端右。
units.en: Wang Guobao curried favor with Prince Daozi while feuding with Wang Xun's circle; fearing feuds after his death, the emperor posted Wang Gong and Xi Hui as governors and left Wang Xun at the capital helm.
units.literal: When Wang Guobao ingratiated himself with Prince Kuaiji Sima Daozi but was not harmonious with Xun and others, the emperor feared that after the imperial carriage's dusk grievance and rifts would surely arise; therefore he sent out Gong and Hui as regional shepherds and entrusted Xun with the right-presidency.

units.zh: 珣夢人以大筆如椽與之，既覺，語人云：「此當有大手筆事。」
units.en: Wang Xun dreamed someone handed him a rafter-sized brush and told friends, "Something momentous will need my pen."
units.literal: Xun dreamed a man gave him a great brush like a rafter; when awakened, he told others, "This means there will be a great-brush affair."

units.zh: 俄而帝崩，哀冊諡議，皆珣所草。
units.en: Soon the emperor died; Wang Xun drafted every lament, patent, and posthumous memorial.
units.literal: Soon the emperor died; lament documents, posthumous patents, and deliberations—were all drafted by Xun.

units.zh: 隆安初，國寶用事，謀黜舊臣，遷珣尚書令。
units.en: Early in Longan, Wang Guobao purged elders and moved Wang Xun up to director of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: At the beginning of Longan, Guobao held power and plotted to dismiss old ministers; Xun was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 王恭赴山陵，欲殺國寶，珣止之曰：「國寶雖終爲禍亂，要罪逆未彰，今便先事而發，必大失朝野之望。
units.en: Wang Gong meant to kill Wang Guobao at the imperial tombs; Wang Xun stopped him, saying, "Although Guobao will ultimately bring disaster, his guilt is not yet plain; move now and we will lose all support at court and in the countryside.
units.literal: Wang Gong went to the imperial tombs and wished to kill Guobao; Xun stopped him, saying, "Although Guobao will ultimately be disaster and disorder, crucially his crime and rebellion are not yet manifest; if now we rise beforehand, we will greatly lose court and countryside expectation.

units.zh: 況擁強兵，竊發於京輦，誰謂非逆！
units.en: Marching on the capital unbidden—who would call that anything but treason?
units.literal: Moreover holding strong troops, secretly rising in the capital region—who would say it is not rebellion!

units.zh: 國寶若遂不改，惡布天下，然後順時望除之，亦無尤不濟也。」
units.en: Wait until Guobao's guilt is universal, then strike with popular backing—you will succeed without blame."
units.literal: If Guobao indeed does not reform, evil spreads under Heaven; afterward following season's expectation removing him—also without blame and not unsuccessful."

units.zh: 恭乃止。
units.en: Wang Gong held his hand.
units.literal: Gong then stopped.

units.zh: 既而謂珣曰：「比來視君，一似胡廣。」
units.en: Later Wang Gong told Wang Xun, "Lately you remind me of Hu Guang."
units.literal: Afterward he said to Xun, "Of late viewing you, altogether like Hu Guang."

units.zh: 旬曰：「王陵廷爭，陳平慎默，但問歳終何如耳。」
units.en: Wang Xun answered, "Wang Ling quarreled in open court; Chen Ping stayed silent—wait and see how the year ends."
units.literal: Xun said, "Wang Ling remonstrated in court; Chen Ping was cautious and silent—only ask how the year-end turns out."

units.zh: 恭尋起兵，國寶將殺珣等，僅而得免，語在國寶傳。
units.en: Wang Gong rose anyway; Wang Guobao nearly executed Wang Xun—see Guobao's biography.
units.literal: Gong soon raised troops; Guobao was about to kill Xun and others; barely they escaped—words are in Guobao's biography.

units.zh: 二年，恭復舉兵，假珣節，進衞將軍、都督琅邪水陸軍事。
units.en: The next year Wang Gong rebelled again; Wang Xun received credentials as general who guards and commander of Langye forces.
units.literal: In the second year, Gong again raised troops; Xun was lent a credential staff, promoted General Who Guards and Commander of Langye land and water forces.

units.zh: 事平，上所假節，加散騎常侍。
units.en: After peace returned he surrendered his staff and added cavalier attendant.
units.literal: When affairs were settled, he returned the lent staff to the emperor; he was added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 四年，以疾解職。
units.en: In the fourth year illness forced him to retire.
units.literal: In the fourth year, because of illness he resigned office.

units.zh: 歳餘，卒，時年五十二。
units.en: A little over a year later he died at fifty-two.
units.literal: After more than a year he died; at the time age fifty-two.

units.zh: 追贈車騎將軍、開府，諡曰獻穆。
units.en: He was posthumously named General of Chariots and Cavalry with independent command and the posthumous epithet Xianmu.
units.literal: Posthumously gifted General of Chariots and Cavalry, establishment of a separate office; posthumous title Xianmu.

units.zh: 桓玄與會稽王道子書曰：「珣神情朗悟，經史明徹，風流之美，公私所寄。
units.en: Huan Xuan wrote Prince Daozi of Kuaiji, saying, "Wang Xun combines brilliance, erudition, and charm—the court and private life alike lean on him.
units.literal: Huan Xuan wrote Prince Kuaiji Sima Daozi a letter, saying, "Xun's spirit and bearing are bright and perceptive; classics and histories are clear and thorough; the beauty of refinement—public and private rely on him.

units.zh: 雖逼嫌謗，才用不盡；
units.en: Slander cramped him, yet his gifts were never fully spent;
units.literal: Although pressed by suspicion and slander, his talent was not fully used;

units.zh: 然君子在朝，弘益自多。
units.en: still, virtuous ministers enlarge any reign.
units.literal: yet when gentlemen are at court, enlarging benefit is naturally abundant.

units.zh: 時事艱難，忽爾喪失，歎懼之深，豈但風流相悼而已！
units.en: These hard times have robbed us of him—Our grief runs deeper than fashionable regret!
units.literal: Times' affairs are difficult; suddenly thus lost—depth of sigh and fear—is it only refinement mourning each other!

units.zh: 其崎嶇九折，風霜備經，雖賴明公神鑒，亦識會居之故也。
units.en: He threaded every hardship—you saw him clearly, sire, and knew what kept him at court.
units.literal: His rugged nine bends, wind and frost fully experienced—although relying on Your Grace's divine mirror, also it is knowing meeting-place's cause.

units.zh: 卒以壽終，殆無所哀。
units.en: If he had died old and full of years, grief would be slight.
units.literal: He ended by dying full years—almost nothing to mourn.

units.zh: 但情發去來，置之未易耳。」
units.en: Yet hearts cling—letting go is hard."
units.literal: Only emotion arises coming and going—setting it aside is not easy."

units.zh: 玄輔政，改贈司徒。
units.en: When Huan Xuan held power he raised Wang Xun's posthumous rank to minister of education.
units.literal: When Xuan assisted governance, posthumous gifts were changed to Minister of Education.

units.zh: 初，珣既與謝安有隙，在東聞安薨，便出京師，詣族弟獻之，曰：「吾欲哭謝公。」
units.en: Though Wang Xun had feuded with Xie An, when word reached him he hurried to the capital and told his cousin Wang Xianzhi, "I must mourn Duke Xie."
units.literal: At first, after Xun already had a rift with Xie An, when in the east he heard An died, then he went out to the capital, visited cousin Xianzhi, and said, "I wish to weep for Duke Xie."

units.zh: 獻之驚曰：「所望於法護。」
units.en: Wang Xianzhi exclaimed, "This is the largeness we expect of Fahu."
units.literal: Xianzhi said in alarm, "What was hoped from Fahu."

units.zh: 於是直前哭之甚慟。
units.en: Wang Xun stepped forward and wept bitterly.
units.literal: Thereupon he went straight forward and wept for him very bitterly.

units.zh: 法護，珣小字也。
units.en: Fahu was Wang Xun's childhood name.
units.literal: Fahu was Xun's childhood name.

units.zh: 珣五子：弘、虞、柳、孺、曇首，宋世並有高名。
units.en: Wang Xun's five sons—Hong, Yu, Liu, Ru, and Tanshou—all rose to fame under Liu Song.
units.literal: Xun had five sons: Hong, Yu, Liu, Ru, and Tanshou—in Song times together had high renown.

units.zh: 珣弟 瑉
units.en: Wang Min, younger brother of Wang Xun
units.literal: Xun's younger brother Min.

units.zh: 瑉字季琰。
units.en: His courtesy name was Jiyan.
units.literal: Min, courtesy name Jiyan.

units.zh: 少有才藝，善行書，名出珣右。
units.en: He showed talent early and surpassed even Wang Xun in running script.
units.literal: In youth he had talent and arts; he was good at running script; his fame exceeded Xun's.

units.zh: 時人爲之語曰：「法護非不佳，僧彌難爲兄。」
units.en: The rhyme ran: "Fahu is fine—but how can anyone be elder brother to Sengmi?"
units.literal: Men of the time made a saying for them: "Fahu is not not good—Sengmi is hard to be elder brother to."

units.zh: 僧彌，瑉小字也。
units.en: Sengmi was Wang Min's pet name.
units.literal: Sengmi was Min's childhood name.

units.zh: 時有外國沙門，名提婆，妙解法理，爲珣兄弟講《毗曇經》。
units.en: The monk Deva from abroad lectured the brothers on the Abhidharma.
units.literal: At that time there was a foreign śramaṇa named Deva, subtly understanding dharma principles, who for Xun and brothers lectured the Abhidharma sutra.

units.zh: 瑉時尚幼，講未半，便雲已解，即於別室與沙門法綱等數人自講。
units.en: While still a boy Wang Min, before the lecture was half finished, said he already understood, and immediately lectured himself in another room with the śramaṇa Fa Gang and several others.
units.literal: Min was still young; before the lecture was half, then he said he already understood; immediately in a separate chamber with śramaṇa Fa Gang and several others he lectured himself.

units.zh: 法綱歎曰：「大義皆是，但小未精耳。」
units.en: Fa Gang sighed, "The outlines are right—the boy needs polish."
units.literal: Fa Gang sighed and said, "The great meaning is all correct, only the small is not yet refined."

units.zh: 辟州主簿，舉秀才，不行。
units.en: He declined provincial chief clerk and flourishing talent nominations.
units.literal: He was summoned as Provincial Chief Clerk; nominated Flourishing Talent; he did not go.

units.zh: 後曆著作、散騎郎、國子博士、黃門侍郎、侍中，代王獻之爲長兼中書令。
units.en: He later served as editorial director, cavalier gentleman, academy erudite, yellow gates, palace attendant, then succeeded Wang Xianzhi as acting palace director.
units.literal: Afterward he passed through Editorial Director, Cavalier Gentleman, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, Palace Attendant, replacing Wang Xianzhi as provisional concurrent Director of the Palace Writers.

units.zh: 二人素齊名，世謂獻之爲「大令」，瑉爲「小令」。
units.en: Both were famed calligraphers—people called Xianzhi the "Great Director" and Min the "Little Director."
units.literal: The two men since youth shared equal name; the age calls Xianzhi "Great Director," Min "Little Director."

units.zh: 太元十三年卒，時年三十八，追贈太常。
units.en: In the thirteenth year of Taiyuan, he died at thirty-eight and was honored posthumously as minister of ceremonies.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Taiyuan, he died; at the time age thirty-eight; posthumously gifted Minister of Ceremonies.

units.zh: 二子：朗、練。
units.en: His sons were Wang Lang and Wang Lian.
units.literal: Two sons: Lang and Lian.

units.zh: 義熙中，並歷侍中。
units.en: Both rose to palace attendant under Yixi.
units.literal: In the Yixi era, both passed through Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 洽弟 協
units.en: Wang Xie, younger brother of Wang Qia
units.literal: [Typographical section label: Qia's younger brother Xie (Wang Xie)]

units.zh: 協字敬祖，元帝撫軍參軍，襲爵武岡侯，早卒，無子，以弟劭子謐爲嗣。
units.en: Wang Xie, courtesy Jingzu, served as adjutant on the pacification army, inherited the Wugang marquisate, died young without issue—his nephew Wang Mi succeeded.
units.literal: Xie, courtesy name Jingzu, was Army Adjutant to Emperor Yuan's general Who Pacifies the Army; he inherited noble rank as Marquis of Wugang; died early without sons; younger brother Shao's son Mi was made heir.

units.zh: 協繼子 謐
units.en: Wang Mi, adopted heir of Wang Xie
units.literal: Xie's adopted heir Mi.

units.zh: 謐字稚遠。
units.en: His courtesy name was Zhiyuan.
units.literal: Mi, courtesy name Zhiyuan.

units.zh: 少有美譽，與譙國桓胤、太原王綏齊名。
units.en: He won praise young alongside Huan Yin and Wang Sui.
units.literal: In youth he had fine reputation; together with Huan Yin of Qiao and Wang Sui of Taiyuan he shared equal name.

units.zh: 拜秘書郎，襲父爵，遷秘書丞，歷中軍長史、黃門郎、侍中。
units.en: He served as palace librarian, inherited his father's title, rose to assistant librarian, then central army clerk, yellow gates, and palace attendant.
units.literal: He was appointed Gentleman of the Palace Library; inherited father's noble rank; transferred to Assistant Supervisor of the Palace Library; passed through Senior Clerk of Central Army, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 及桓玄舉兵，詔謐銜命詣玄，玄深敬昵焉。
units.en: When Huan Xuan rebelled, Wang Mi carried imperial orders to him and won deep favor.
units.literal: When Huan Xuan raised troops, an edict ordered Mi to bear mission and go to Xuan; Xuan deeply revered and was intimate with him.

units.zh: 拜建威將軍、呉國內史，未至郡，玄以爲中書令、領軍將軍、吏部尚書，遷中書監，加散騎常侍，領司徒。
units.en: Named general who establishes might and Wu interior clerk, he never reached the post—Huan Xuan kept him as palace director, commander, minister of personnel, then palace supervisor, cavalier attendant, and minister of education.
units.literal: He was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Interior Clerk of Wu; before reaching the commandery, Xuan made him Director of the Palace Writers, Army Commander General, Minister of Personnel; transferred to Supervisor of the Palace Writers, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrent Minister of Education.

units.zh: 及玄將篡，以謐兼太保，奉璽冊詣玄。
units.en: At Huan Xuan's coup Wang Mi served as grand mentor and carried the imperial seal to him.
units.literal: When Xuan was about to usurp, he made Mi concurrent Grand Mentor, bearing seal and patent to go to Xuan.

units.zh: 玄篡，封武昌縣開國公，加班劍二十人。
units.en: After the usurpation he became founding duke of Wuchang county with twenty sword guards.
units.literal: When Xuan usurped, Mi was enfeoffed Duke Who Founded Wuchang county, added twenty sword attendants.

units.zh: 初，劉裕爲布衣，眾未之識也，惟謐獨奇貴之，嘗謂裕曰：「卿當爲一代英雄。」
units.en: Once when Liu Yu was unknown, only Wang Mi marked him as extraordinary—"You will be the hero of your age," he said.
units.literal: At first when Liu Yu was plain cloth, the multitude did not recognize him—only Mi alone thought him singularly noble; he once said to Yu, "You will surely become a generation's hero."

units.zh: 及裕破恆玄，謐以本官加侍中，領揚州刺史、録尚書事。
units.en: After Liu Yu smashed Huan Xuan, Wang Mi kept rank while adding palace attendant, Yangzhou inspector, and recorder of Masters of Writing.
units.literal: When Yu defeated Huan Xuan, Mi with original offices added Palace Attendant, concurrent Inspector of Yang Province and Recorder of Masters-of-Writing Affairs.

units.zh: 謐既受寵桓氏，常不自安。
units.en: His past closeness to the Huans left him uneasy.
units.literal: Mi having received favor from the Huan clan, constantly was not at ease.

units.zh: 護軍將軍劉毅嘗問謐曰：「璽綬何在？」
units.en: Liu Yi once demanded, "Where is the imperial seal?"
units.literal: Protecting Army General Liu Yi once asked Mi, "Where are seal and ribbon?"

units.zh: 謐益懼。
units.en: Wang Mi grew terrified.
units.literal: Mi grew more fearful.

units.zh: 會王綏以桓氏甥自疑，謀反，父子兄弟皆伏誅。
units.en: Then Wang Sui, Huan's nephew by marriage, rebelled and his whole clan died.
units.literal: When Wang Sui because he was Huan clan's nephew suspected himself, plotted rebellion—father and sons and brothers all were executed.

units.zh: 謐從弟諶，少驍果輕俠，欲誘謐還呉，起兵爲亂，乃説謐曰：「王綏無罪，而義旗誅之，是除時望也。
units.en: His cousin Wang Chen, rash and martial, urged Wang Mi to flee east: "Wang Sui was without crime, yet the righteous banner executed him—this is removing the eminent of the age.
units.literal: Mi's cousin Chen, in youth bold and decisive as roaming knight, wished to entice Mi back to Wu and raise troops making rebellion; then he persuaded Mi, saying, "Wang Sui was without crime, yet the righteous banner executed him—this is removing the age's expectation.

units.zh: 兄少立名譽，加位地如此，欲不危，得乎！」
units.en: You stand too high to stay safe—flight is the only choice!"
units.literal: Elder brother from youth established fame and reputation, plus position and station thus—wishing not to be in peril—is it possible!"

units.zh: 謐懼而出奔。
units.en: Terrified, Wang Mi bolted.
units.literal: Mi feared and fled.

units.zh: 劉裕箋詣大將軍、武陵王遵，遣人追躡，謐既還，委任如先，加謐班劍二十人。
units.en: Liu Yu appealed to Prince Sima Zun to recall him; Wang Mi returned to favor with twenty sword attendants.
units.literal: Liu Yu sent a note to Grand General Prince Wuling Zun, dispatching men to pursue on trail; after Mi returned, trust and employment were as before; Mi was added twenty sword attendants.

units.zh: 義熙三年卒，時年四十八。
units.en: In the third year of Yixi, he died at forty-eight.
units.literal: In the third year of Yixi, he died; at the time age forty-eight.

units.zh: 追贈侍中、司徒，諡曰文恭。
units.en: Posthumously he was palace attendant and minister of education with the epithet Cultured and Respectful.
units.literal: Posthumously gifted Palace Attendant and Minister of Education; posthumous title was Wen Gong.

units.zh: 三子：瓘、球、琇。
units.en: His sons were Wang Guan, Wang Qiu, and Wang Xiu.
units.literal: Three sons: Guan, Qiu, and Xiu.

units.zh: 入宋，皆至大官。
units.en: Under Liu Song all rose to high office.
units.literal: Entering Song, all reached great offices.

units.zh: 協弟劭
units.en: Wang Shao, younger brother of Wang Xie
units.literal: [Typographical section label: Xie's younger brother Shao (Wang Shao)]

units.zh: 劭字敬倫，歷東陽太守、吏部郎、司徒左長史、丹陽尹。
units.en: Wang Shao, courtesy Jinglun, served as prefect of Dongyang, personnel gentleman, ministry senior clerk, and governor of Danyang.
units.literal: Shao, courtesy name Jinglun, passed through Prefect of Dongyang, Gentleman of Personnel Ministry, Senior Clerk of Minister of Education's Left, Governor of Danyang.

units.zh: 劭美姿容，有風操，雖家人近習，未嘗見其墜替之容。
units.en: Handsome and composed, he never showed slack conduct even before servants.
units.literal: Shao's bearing was beautiful; he had manner and integrity; although family members and intimate attendants, never did they see his fallen-substitute expression.

units.zh: 桓溫甚器之。
units.en: Huan Wen held him in high regard.
units.literal: Huan Wen greatly esteemed him.

units.zh: 遷吏部尚書、尚書僕射，領中領軍，出爲建威將軍、呉國內史。
units.en: He rose to minister of personnel, vice director of Masters of Writing, central army commander, then general who establishes might and Wu interior clerk.
units.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Personnel, Vice Director of Masters of Writing, concurrent Central Army Commander; went out as General Who Establishes Might and Interior Clerk of Wu.

units.zh: 卒，贈車騎將軍，諡曰簡。
units.en: He died honored as general of chariots and cavalry with the epithet Austere.
units.literal: When he died, he was gifted General of Chariots and Cavalry; posthumous title Jian.

units.zh: 三子：穆、默、恢。
units.en: His sons were Wang Mu, Wang Mo, and Wang Hui.
units.literal: Three sons: Mu, Mo, and Hui.

units.zh: 穆，臨海太守。
units.en: Wang Mu governed Linhai.
units.literal: Mu was Prefect of Linhai.

units.zh: 默，呉國內史，加二千石。
units.en: Wang Mo served as Wu interior clerk at two thousand shi salary.
units.literal: Mo was Interior Clerk of Wu, added two thousand shi.

units.zh: 恢，右衞將軍。
units.en: Wang Hui became general of the right guards.
units.literal: Hui was General of the Right Guards.

units.zh: 穆三子：簡、智、超。
units.en: Wang Mu's sons were Jian, Zhi, and Chao.
units.literal: Mu's three sons: Jian, Zhi, and Chao.

units.zh: 默二子：鑒、惠。
units.en: Wang Mo's sons were Jian and Hui.
units.literal: Mo's two sons: Jian and Hui.

units.zh: 義熙中，並曆顯職。
units.en: During Yixi they all reached prominent posts.
units.literal: In the Yixi era, together they passed through eminent offices.

units.zh: 劭弟 薈
units.en: Wang Hui, younger brother of Wang Shao
units.literal: [Typographical section label: Shao's younger brother Hui (Wang Hui)]

units.zh: 薈字敬文。
units.en: His courtesy name was Jingwen.
units.literal: Hui, courtesy name Jingwen.

units.zh: 恬虛守靖，不競榮利，少曆清官，除吏部郎、侍中、建威將軍、呉國內史。
units.en: He lived quietly without ambition, served in unsullied posts, and rose to personnel gentleman, palace attendant, general who establishes might, and Wu interior clerk.
units.literal: He was tranquil-empty guarding quietude, not competing for glory and profit; in youth passed through pure offices; appointed Gentleman of Personnel Ministry, Palace Attendant, General Who Establishes Might, Interior Clerk of Wu.

units.zh: 時年饑粟貴，人多餓死，薈以私米作饘粥，以飴餓者，所濟活甚眾。
units.en: When famine struck he brewed gruel from his own grain and saved countless lives.
units.literal: At that time there was famine and grain was dear; many people starved to death; Hui used private grain to make gruel porridge to feed the starving—those rescued and kept alive were very many.

units.zh: 征補中領軍，不拜。
units.en: He declined appointment as central army commander.
units.literal: He was summoned to supplement Central Army Commander; he did not accept.

units.zh: 徙尚書，領中護軍，復爲征虜將軍、呉國內史。
units.en: He moved to the Masters of Writing with protecting army command, then general who subdues brigands and Wu interior clerk.
units.literal: He was shifted to Masters of Writing, concurrent Protecting Army Commander; again became General Who Subdues Brigands and Interior Clerk of Wu.

units.zh: 頃之，桓沖表請薈爲江州刺史，固辭不拜。
units.en: Huan Chong nominated him for Jiangzhou; Wang Hui refused.
units.literal: Shortly, Huan Chong memorialized requesting Hui as Inspector of Jiang Province; he firmly declined and did not accept.

units.zh: 轉督浙江東五郡、左將軍、會稽內史，進號鎮軍將軍，加散騎常侍。
units.en: He supervised five eastern commanderies as general of the left and Kuaiji interior clerk, took the banner general who guards the army, and added cavalier attendant.
units.literal: He was transferred to supervise east of Zhejiang five commanderies, General of the Left and Interior Clerk of Kuaiji; advanced title General Who Guards the Army, added Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 卒于官，贈衞將軍。
units.en: He died in harness and was honored as general who guards.
units.literal: He died in office; gifted General Who Guards.

units.zh: 薈子 廞
units.en: Wang Xu, son of Wang Hui
units.literal: Hui's son Xu.

units.zh: 子廞，歷太子中庶子、司徒左長史。
units.en: Wang Xu served as deputy to the heir and senior clerk under the minister of education.
units.literal: Son Xu passed through Palace Deputy to the Heir Apparent and Senior Clerk of Minister of Education's Left.

units.zh: 以母喪，居於呉。
units.en: Mourning his mother, he stayed in Wu.
units.literal: Because of mother's mourning, he dwelt in Wu.

units.zh: 王恭舉兵，假廞建武將軍、呉國內史，令起軍，助爲聲援。
units.en: When Wang Gong rebelled he named Wang Xu general who establishes martial might and Wu interior clerk, ordering him to mobilize in support.
units.literal: When Wang Gong raised troops, Xu was lent General Who Establishes Martial Might and Interior Clerk of Wu; he was ordered to raise troops and assist as sounding aid.

units.zh: 廞即墨絰合眾，誅殺異己，仍遣前呉國內史虞嘯父等入呉興、義興聚兵，輕俠赴者萬計。
units.en: Wang Xu, still in mourning garb, rallied troops, purged dissenters, and sent Yu Xiaofu into Wuxing and Yixing—thousands of adventurers answered.
units.literal: Xu then in ink mourning sash gathered hosts, executed and killed those not of his party; still dispatched former Interior Clerk of Wu Yu Xiaofu and others into Wuxing and Yixing to gather troops—light-knight followers who came numbered in tens of thousands.

units.zh: 廞自謂義兵一動，勢必未寧，可乘間而取富貴。
units.en: Wang Xu gambled that rebellion would unsettle the realm and open a path to power.
units.literal: Xu himself thought that once righteous troops moved, the situation would surely not be settled—one could exploit gaps and seize wealth and honor.

units.zh: 而曾不旬日，國寶賜死，恭罷兵符，廞去職。
units.en: Within days Wang Guobao was forced to suicide, Wang Gong lost his command, and Wang Xu was dismissed.
units.literal: Yet not even ten days had passed—Guobao was gifted death; Gong was stripped of military tally; Xu left office.

units.zh: 廞大怒，回眾討恭。
units.en: Enraged, Wang Xu wheeled his army against Wang Gong.
units.literal: Xu was greatly angry; he turned his host to campaign against Gong.

units.zh: 恭遣司馬劉牢之距戰于曲阿，廞眾潰奔走，遂不知所在。
units.en: Wang Gong sent Liu Laozhi to meet him at Qu'e; Wang Xu's force broke and scattered and he vanished.
units.literal: Gong dispatched Major Liu Laozhi to oppose battle at Qu'e; Xu's host collapsed and fled running—thereupon his whereabouts were unknown.

units.zh: 長子泰爲恭所殺，少子華以不知廞存亡，憂毀布衣蔬食。
units.en: Wang Gong killed Wang Xu's eldest son Tai; the younger son Hua mourned in hemp and gruel, not knowing whether his father lived.
units.literal: The eldest son Tai was killed by Gong; the younger son Hua because he did not know whether Xu lived or died, in anxious grief wore plain cloth and ate vegetables.

units.zh: 後從兄謐言其死所，華始發喪，入仕。
units.en: Only when cousin Wang Mi revealed where he had died could Hua bury him properly and take office.
units.literal: Afterward elder cousin Mi spoke his place of death; Hua then began mourning observances and entered official service.

units.zh: 初，導渡淮，使郭璞筮之，卦成，璞曰：「吉，無不利。
units.en: When Wang Dao first crossed the Huai, Guo Pu cast the stalks and said, "The omen is wholly favorable.
units.literal: At first, when Dao crossed the Huai, he had Guo Pu divine it; when the hexagram was completed, Pu said, "Auspicious—nothing not favorable.

units.zh: 淮水絶，王氏滅。」
units.en: Yet when the Huai runs dry, the house of Wang will end."
units.literal: When Huai water is cut off, the Wang clan perishes."

units.zh: 其後子孫繁衍，竟如璞言。
units.en: His descendants multiplied beyond counting—Guo Pu's words proved true.
units.literal: Afterward descendants multiplied and spread—ultimately as Pu had said.

units.zh: 史臣曰==
units.en: (Historian's commentary)
units.literal: [Section heading: Historian's commentary]

units.zh: 史臣曰：飛龍御天，故資雲雨之勢；
units.en: The historians write: The dragon rides the storm—no ascent without clouds and rain.
units.literal: The historians say: The flying dragon mounts Heaven—therefore it relies on cloud-and-rain momentum;

units.zh: 帝王興運，必俟股肱之力。
units.en: Every throne waits on ministers strong as thighs and arms.
units.literal: when imperial kings raise their fortune, they must await thigh-and-arm strength.

units.zh: 軒轅，聖人也，杖師臣而授圖；
units.en: The Yellow Emperor leaned on his ministers to read Heaven's chart;
units.literal: The Gray Emperor was a sage—leaning on his minister-vassal he received the chart;

units.zh: 商湯，哲后也，托負鼎而成業。
units.en: King Tang of Shang built his realm on ministers who bore the sacred bronzes.
units.literal: Shang Tang was a wise sovereign—entrusting the cauldron-bearing he completed his enterprise.

units.zh: 自斯已降，罔不由之。
units.en: Every dynasty since has done the same.
units.literal: From this downward, none has not followed this.

units.zh: 原夫典午發蹤，本於陵寡，金行撫運，無德在時。
units.en: The house of Sima seized power by bullying an orphan; Jin's "metal" mandate arrived without moral warrant.
units.literal: Tracing how the Archives-Horse rose—rooted in overriding the orphan—Metal Phase soothing fortune lacked virtue in its season.

units.zh: 九土未宅其心，四夷已承其弊。
units.en: The realm never warmed to the throne while borders already felt its decay.
units.literal: The nine soils had not settled their hearts; the four barbarians already endured its harm.

units.zh: 既而中原蕩覆，江左嗣興，兆著玄石之圖，乖少康之祀夏；
units.en: When the north collapsed, the southeast revival bore dark-stone portents—nothing so clean as Shaokang's restoration of Xia;
units.literal: Soon the central plain was swept away; south of the Yangzi succession rose—omens appeared on black-stone charts, differing from Shaokang's restoring Xia;

units.zh: 時無思晉之士，異文叔之興劉；
units.en: no Han loyalists rallied as they had for Liu Xiu's Han revival;
units.literal: the age had no men yearning for Jin—different from Wendi's raising Liu;

units.zh: 輔佐中宗，艱哉甚矣！
units.en: supporting Emperor Yuan was perilous work.
units.literal: to assist Zhongzong—hard indeed it was!

units.zh: 茂弘策名枝屏，葉情交好，負其才智，恃彼江湖，思建克復之功，用成翌宣之道。
units.en: Wang Dao Maohong pledged himself to the frontier princes, poured heart into friendship, trusted his genius and the Yangzi barrier, and meant to reconquer the north while shaping Jin's mandate.
units.literal: Maohong enlisted his name on branch screens, harmonized feelings in friendship, bore his talent and wisdom, relied on those rivers and lakes, thought to establish merit of recovery and defeat, thereby completing assistance-and-proclaiming Way.

units.zh: 於是王敦內侮，憑天邑而狼顧；
units.en: Then Wang Dun turned wolfishly on the capital;
units.literal: Thereupon Wang Dun inwardly insulted, leaning on the celestial city and wolf-glancing;

units.zh: 蘇峻連兵，指宸居而隼擊。
units.en: Su Jun struck the throne like a stooping hawk.
units.literal: Su Jun linked troops, pointing at the polar dwelling and falcon-striking.

units.zh: 實賴元宰，固懷匪石之心；
units.en: Only the chief minister's faith—unyielding as the ode's pledge—
units.literal: Truly relying on the chief minister—firmly harboring not-stone heart;

units.zh: 潛運忠謨，竟翦吞沙之寇。
units.en: and silent stratagem rooted out those rebels.
units.literal: secretly wielded loyal stratagem—finally cut down sand-swallowing bandits.

units.zh: 乃誠貫日，主垂餌以終全；
units.en: His devotion shone through—the emperor cast trust like bait and kept him whole;
units.literal: Thus sincerity pierced the sun; the lord hung bait and thereby ended whole;

units.zh: 貞志陵霜，國綴旒而不滅。
units.en: his steadfast heart outlasted frost—though the crown slipped, the house endured.
units.literal: steadfast intent exceeded frost—the state hung tassels yet did not perish.

units.zh: 觀其開設學校，存乎沸鼎之中，爰立章程，在乎櫛風之際；
units.en: He founded schools while the cauldron boiled and drafted laws while wind combed his hair;
units.literal: Observe him establishing schools, preserving them amid boiling cauldron; then setting statutes and measures, in wind-combing moments;

units.zh: 雖則世道多故，而規模弘遠矣。
units.en: through chaos his vision stayed immense.
units.literal: although the age's way had many vicissitudes, yet the scope was vast and far-reaching.

units.zh: 比夫蕭曹弼漢，六合爲家；
units.en: Xiao He and Cao Shen folded the realm into one family;
units.literal: Compared to Xiao and Cao assisting Han—the six directions became one household;

units.zh: 奭望匡周，萬方同軌，功未半古，不足爲儔。
units.en: Shi and Wang lined every wagon-track—Wang Dao matches neither half their deed.
units.literal: Shi and Wang rectifying Zhou—myriad regions shared one track—his merit does not reach half antiquity; insufficient to be paired.

units.zh: 至若夷吾體仁，能相小國；
units.en: Guan Zhong embodied humanity in a small state;
units.literal: As for Yiwu embodying benevolence—able to minister to a small state;

units.zh: 孔明踐義，善翊新邦，撫事論情，抑斯之類也。
units.en: Zhuge Liang upheld duty in a new realm—Wang Dao belongs in their company.
units.literal: Kongming treading righteousness—well aiding a new domain handling affairs discussing sentiment—perhaps this category.

units.zh: 提挈三世，終始一心，稱爲「仲父」，蓋其宜矣。
units.en: Three reigns hung on one loyal heart—no wonder men called him "Second Father."
units.literal: He raised three generations; beginning and end one heart—styled "Second Father"—indeed fitting.

units.zh: 恬珣踵德，副呂虔之贈刀；
units.en: Wang Tian and Wang Xun inherited honor worthy of Lü Qian's sword;
units.literal: Tian and Xun followed virtue—matching Lü Qian's gifting sword;

units.zh: 謐乃聵聲，慚劉毅之征璽。
units.en: Wang Mi played deaf when Liu Yi demanded the seal—a shame beside them.
units.literal: Mi then was deaf to reputation—ashamed before Liu Yi's demanding seal.

units.zh: 語曰：「深山大澤，有龍有蛇。」
units.en: The proverb holds: "Deep hills breed dragons—and snakes."
units.literal: A saying goes: "In deep mountains and great marshes there are dragons and serpents."

units.zh: 實斯之謂也。
units.en: So it proved for this clan.
units.literal: Truly this is what it speaks of.

units.zh: 贊曰：虎嘯猋馳，龍升雲映。
units.en: The ode runs: Tigers roar on the wind; dragons climb through clouds;
units.literal: The encomium says: Tigers roar and whirlwind gallops; dragons ascend clouds reflecting.

units.zh: 武岡矯矯，匡時輯政。
units.en: the Wugang line stands tall, steadying the age and gathering the state.
units.literal: Wugang lofty-lofty—rectifies the age and gathers governance.

units.zh: 懿績克宣，忠規靡競。
units.en: Their deeds shine forth; loyalty leaves no rival.
units.literal: Splendid deeds are able to proclaim; loyal norms without strife.

units.zh: 契葉三主，榮逾九命。
units.en: They matched hearts with three sovereigns and won honors beyond nine bestowals.
units.literal: Their covenant harmonized three lords; glory exceeded nine commands.

units.zh: 貽刀表祥，巫水流慶。
units.en: Swords passed hand to hand foretold fortune; the Wu streams ran thick with blessing.
units.literal: The transmitted sword showed auspice; Wu waters flow blessing.

units.zh: 赫矣門族，重光斯盛。
units.en: How bright this house—its glory redoubled again and again.
units.literal: Bright indeed the clan—doubled radiance thus flourishes.
